steps.text: Walk out of your house when Navi stops shouting and climb down the ladder to the grass.
steps.detail: The opening nightmare and Navi's flight over the village play first. You take control standing inside the treehouse; the ladder is straight out the front door.

steps.text: Talk to Saria waiting at the foot of the ladder.
steps.detail: She only cheers your new fairy and sends you to the Great Deku Tree. Skippable, but she stands right in your path.

steps.text: Walk southwest across the village to the fenced Forest Training Center, the bottom-left corner of the map.
steps.detail: Follow the grass past Mido's House and up the slope. The Training Center is the low fenced pen with a sign on the wall.

steps.text: Face the small hole in the wall beside the sign, press A to crawl in and hold forward until you pop out the far side.
steps.detail: This crawlspace is the only way into the sword maze.

steps.text: Round the first corner and pick up the Blue Rupee lying there.
steps.detail: Worth 5. Every maze rupee comes back if you leave the Training Center and walk in again.

steps.text: Wait against the wall for the giant rolling boulder to pass, then fall in behind it and take the first passage on the right.
steps.detail: The boulder loops the maze on a fixed track and knocks you flat on contact. Following close behind it always gives you the full loop of clearance.

steps.text: Grab the second Blue Rupee in that right-hand passage.
Step back out behind the boulder and carry on to the next alcove along the maze.
steps.detail: Wait for the boulder to come round again if you are not sure you can beat it to the alcove.

steps.text: Open the large chest in the alcove for the Kokiri Sword.
Pause, open the Equipment screen and select the Kokiri Sword to equip it.
steps.detail: The sword goes on the B button. On Switch Online, press Start to pause and the shoulder buttons to reach the Equipment page.

steps.text: Follow the maze back around to the crawl hole and crawl out into the Training Center.
steps.detail: Keep watching for the boulder on the way back; it runs the same track.

steps.text: Talk to the Kokiri boy just outside the crawl hole, then Z-target the rock and backflip by holding back and pressing A.
steps.detail: He teaches the backflip and the spot pays rupees. You need 40 Rupees for the shield, and every loose rupee in the village respawns if you duck into a house and come back out.

steps.text: Go into Mido's House, the building directly across from the crawl hole, and open the chests inside for rupees.
Walk around the back of Mido's House and pick up the Blue Rupee hidden there.
Climb the ramp beside Saria's House, next door to your own, and follow it toward the middle of the village for the rupee at the top.
Run across the two stone platforms in the water between Mido's House and the shop; Link hops them on his own and collects 5 rupees.
steps.detail: Repeat these spots, re-entering a house between laps, until your wallet reads 40.

steps.text: Enter the Kokiri Shop, the building in the northeast corner of the village.
steps.detail: The girl sitting above the doorway is the Z-targeting tutorial: press Z to lock on, A to talk. Nothing is lost by walking past her.

steps.text: Pick up the hidden Blue Rupee tucked against the side wall of the shop.
Step up to the counter and buy the Deku Shield for 40 Rupees.
Pause, open the Equipment screen and equip the Deku Shield alongside the Kokiri Sword.
steps.detail: Mido checks for both equipped. Owning them is not enough; he keeps refusing until they are on Link's back.

steps.text: Leave the shop and talk to Mido, who is blocking the north path out of the village.
steps.detail: He insults you and then steps aside.

steps.text: Follow the narrow path north toward the Great Deku Tree.
Slash the three Withered Deku Babas near the end of the path and pick up the Deku Sticks they drop.
steps.detail: They never move and never attack; one slash each. The sticks are your only way to light a torch in the dungeon.

steps.text: Talk to the Great Deku Tree and answer Yes when he asks whether you are willing to break his curse.
Walk into the Great Deku Tree's open mouth to enter the dungeon.
Kill the Deku Babas growing out of the floor of the 1F entrance room.
steps.detail: Z-target one, hold R to block its lunge, then slash as it snaps back. They drop Deku Nuts. Slash the weeds for Recovery Hearts if you got bitten; they grow back. Leave the big web in the middle of the floor alone, you break it later from above.

steps.text: Pause and assign Deku Sticks and Deku Nuts to your C buttons.
steps.detail: Without them on C you cannot light a torch or throw a nut, and both come up within minutes.

steps.text: Climb the wooden ladder on the side of the tower up to the 2F ledge.
steps.detail: The vines beside it work just as well. Navi stops you to explain climbing.

steps.text: Follow the 2F ledge clockwise and open the large chest on it for the Dungeon Map.
steps.detail: You pass a patch of vines with Skullwalltulas crawling on them just before the chest. Leave them; you come back with the Slingshot.

steps.text: Keep going right along the 2F ledge, jumping the gaps, until you reach the last platform.
Go through the door at the end of the 2F ledge.
Z-target the Deku Scrub and hold R so the nut it spits bounces off your shield and stuns it.
steps.detail: Stay several paces back or it ducks into its hole before it fires.

steps.text: Run the stunned Scrub down and talk to it before it burrows.
steps.detail: Its hint is the landing roll: hold the stick forward as you touch down from a long fall. It leaves Recovery Hearts and the far door opens.

steps.text: Go through the door that opened on the far side of the room.
Take a running jump across the crumbling middle platform to the far ledge.
steps.detail: The platform starts falling the moment you land on it, so do not stop. If you drop into the pit, climb the wall vines back up.

steps.text: Open the large chest on the ledge for the Fairy Slingshot.
steps.detail: The dungeon's main item. Its ammo is Deku Seeds, which drop from slashed bushes.

steps.text: Climb the vines beside the chest to the hidden alcove and open the small chest for a Recovery Heart.
Face the entry door, Z-target the ladder hanging on the wall above it and shoot it down with the Fairy Slingshot.
steps.detail: The platform you jumped from is gone, so the dropped ladder is the only way back out.

steps.text: Climb the ladder and go back through the door to the 2F ledge of the main room.
Walk back around 2F to the vines by the Dungeon Map chest and shoot every Skullwalltula off them with the Fairy Slingshot.
steps.detail: Left alive they bite you mid-climb and knock you all the way down to 1F.

steps.text: Climb the vines to the very top, shuffle sideways along them until you hang over the 3F walkway, and let go.
steps.detail: Left or right both work; go far enough that there is solid floor under you before you release.

steps.text: Work along the 3F walkway past the Big Skulltulas hanging over it.
steps.detail: They drop only when you get close. Stand just near enough to bring one down, wait for it to spin and show its soft belly, then slash. You can also shoot the belly from range with the Fairy Slingshot.

steps.text: Go through the door at the end of the 3F walkway.
Step on the floor switch in this room to raise the three sunken platforms.
Hop across the three platforms to the far side of the room before they sink again.
steps.detail: They stay up only a few seconds. If you fall, walk back and hit the switch again.

steps.text: Open the large chest on the far side for the Compass.
Jump down to the floor of the room and kill the Big Skulltula hanging on the right.
steps.detail: Start of the detour for Gold Skulltula #1. Skip the next six steps if you are not collecting.

steps.text: Kill the Deku Baba growing in front of the vines.
Climb the vines back up to the ledge with the floor switch.
Step on the floor switch a second time to raise the platforms again.
Hop across the platforms to the alcove on the left this time.
Open the small chest in the left alcove for a Recovery Heart.
Kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall behind that chest and touch the Gold Skulltula token it drops.
steps.detail: Slash it or shoot it with the Fairy Slingshot, then walk into the token. First of the 100 tokens in the game.

steps.text: Jump down and climb the vines back up to the ledge with the barred door.
steps.detail: The door you came in by is barred. The two torches beside it are the lock.

steps.text: Take out a Deku Stick and hold it in the lit torch until it catches fire.
Carry the burning stick to the unlit torch and stand beside it so the flame jumps across; the bars on the door vanish.
steps.detail: Press B to draw your sword the instant it catches. A lit stick burns to nothing in about ten seconds, and switching weapons puts it away intact.

steps.text: Go back through the unbarred door to the 3F walkway of the main room.
Kill the Big Skulltula guarding the edge of the 3F walkway.
steps.detail: You need that edge clear to line up the jump, or it knocks you off mid-aim.

steps.text: Jump off the edge of 3F and land dead centre on the web on the 1F floor; it tears and drops you into the flooded basement.
steps.detail: Catch only the rim and the web bounces you like a trampoline. Climb all the way back up to 3F and aim again.

steps.text: Look up at the basement vines that lead back to the floor above and shoot the Gold Skulltula crawling on them with the Fairy Slingshot.
Climb the vines and touch the Gold Skulltula token.
Shoot the Gold Skulltula sitting on the grating at the north end of the basement with the Fairy Slingshot.
Climb the platform beside the grating, jump across and take the Gold Skulltula token.
Climb onto the platform in the basement and step on the floor switch; the torch next to it lights and burns off the cobweb covering it.
steps.detail: That torch is the flame source for everything left in the basement, so note where it stands.

steps.text: Light a Deku Stick on the newly lit torch.
Carry the flame across the shallow water to the far platform and burn the cobwebs covering the door.
steps.detail: Keep to the shallow part where Link walks. The moment he starts swimming the flame goes out and you restart at the torch.

steps.text: Go through the door behind the burned cobwebs.
Z-target the Deku Scrub in this room and reflect its nut back with your shield.
steps.detail: Same trick as the first Scrub: hold R and stay back. Slash the bushes here for Deku Seeds if your Slingshot ammo is low.

steps.text: Chase it down before it burrows and listen to its hint: 2, 3, 1.
steps.detail: That is the order for the three-Scrub puzzle at the very bottom of the dungeon. Middle, right, left.

steps.text: Shoot the silver eye switch mounted above the next door with the Fairy Slingshot.
Go through the door the eye switch opened.
Jump into the water and swim to the left side of the room.
steps.detail: Navi stops you here to explain diving.

steps.text: Get over the underwater switch on the bottom, hold A to dive and steer onto it; the water level drops.
steps.detail: Use the stick to swim down and forward. The water stays low only for a short while.

steps.text: Swim back to the first platform and climb the ramp on it.
Wait for the floating platform to drift over to your side and jump onto it.
steps.detail: If the water rises again before you board, dive for the switch once more.

steps.text: Ride the floating platform under the spinning spiked log and climb up on the far side.
steps.detail: Stay in the middle of the raft; the log passes right overhead.

steps.text: Kill the Big Skulltula hanging over this ledge.
Stand against the side of the stone block and push or pull it until it sits directly under the doorway.
steps.detail: Walk into a face of the block and hold A, then push or pull with the stick. Navi explains it the first time.

steps.text: Climb onto the block and go through the door above it.
steps.detail: Walk into the block and press A to pull yourself up.

steps.text: Kill the Deku Baba and the Withered Deku Baba in this room and collect what they drop.
Light a Deku Stick on the one lit torch in the room.
Light the two unlit torches with the burning stick.
steps.detail: Take the nearer one first. The stick only lasts a few seconds after it catches.

steps.text: Go through the door that opens once both torches burn.
Stand in the doorway, Z-target the Big Skulltula straight ahead and shoot it twice with the Fairy Slingshot before you step inside.
steps.detail: From this far back it stays hanging with its soft side turned toward you, so it dies for free.

steps.text: Walk forward past the three shadows in the middle of the room; eggs drop from the ceiling and hatch into Gohma Larvae.
Z-target one Gohma Larva at a time, get close and slash it until all three are dead.
steps.detail: They are only dangerous as a pack. Two sword swipes or one jump attack each.

steps.text: Light a Deku Stick on the torch in this room.
Carry the flame to the cobweb at the far end of the room and burn it.
steps.detail: The other cobweb in here hides a wall you cannot open yet. The Gold Skulltula behind it needs Bombs and is collected in a later chapter.

steps.text: Crawl through the hole behind the burned cobweb.
Push the stone block on this ledge off the edge to open a permanent shortcut back up.
steps.detail: You come out on the upper level of the flooded basement. Kill the Deku Babas up here first if they crowd you.

steps.text: Jump down to the low torch you lit with the floor switch earlier and light a Deku Stick on it.
steps.detail: The two torches up on the ledge are mounted too high to light a stick from.

steps.text: Climb the fallen block back up onto the ledge with the stick still burning.
steps.detail: This is why the block had to go over the edge first; nothing else is fast enough.

steps.text: Burn the cobweb in the floor of the ledge with the lit stick.
steps.detail: Roll into it with A or swing the stick with its C button. Either one sets it alight.

steps.text: Drop through the burned floor into the deepest part of the dungeon.
steps.detail: Dive in the water down here for Recovery Hearts before you take on the boss.

steps.text: Climb out onto the land facing the three Deku Scrubs.
Reflect the middle Deku Scrub's nut back at it first.
steps.detail: This is the 2 in the 2, 3, 1 hint. Stun them out of order and all three reset.

steps.text: Reflect the right-hand Deku Scrub's nut back at it second.
Reflect the left-hand Deku Scrub's nut back at it last; the way to the boss opens.
Catch the last Deku Scrub before it runs off and listen to its hint about the boss.
Go through the boss door.
Look up at Queen Gohma clinging to the ceiling to start the fight.
steps.detail: Nothing happens until you look up. Keep the Fairy Slingshot on a C button.

steps.text: Block her lunge with your shield or sidestep it when she wobbles toward you.
steps.detail: This is her only contact attack and it is slow. Z-target her and hold R.

steps.text: Slash the three eggs she drops from the ceiling before they hatch, and kill any Gohma Larva that gets out.
steps.detail: A larva takes two sword swipes or one jump attack.

steps.text: Shoot her eye with the Fairy Slingshot the instant it glows red; she crashes to the floor.
steps.detail: The eye turns red right before and right after each of her attacks. Stunning her while she is still on the ceiling drops her for far longer than stunning her on the ground, and that is the fastest kill. A Deku Nut stuns her too, but the Slingshot is much easier.

steps.text: Slash her eye with your sword over and over while she lies stunned, then repeat the stun until she disintegrates.
steps.detail: Done cleanly from the ceiling, the whole fight takes under a minute.

steps.text: Take the Heart Container left in her remains.
Step into the blue light to warp out of the dungeon.
Listen to the Great Deku Tree's story about the man from the desert and the three Spiritual Stones.
steps.detail: He explains that the stones open the door to the Sacred Realm and the Triforce, and that the curse laid on him for refusing to hand his over cannot be lifted.

steps.text: Take the Kokiri's Emerald when he gives it to you.
steps.detail: The Spiritual Stone of the Forest, the first of the three.

steps.text: Watch the Great Deku Tree wither, then walk back down the path into Kokiri Forest.
steps.detail: He sends you to find the Princess of Destiny at Hyrule Castle. The next chapter starts at the village exit.

steps.text: Follow the path down out of the Great Deku Tree's meadow into Kokiri Forest village.
steps.detail: You come out at the top of the village, near Mido's house and the shop.

steps.text: Sit through Mido's scene at the bottom of the path.
steps.detail: It plays by itself and you get no reply: he decides you killed the Great Deku Tree and storms off. Nothing else in the village has changed, and no house or shop has anything you need right now.

steps.text: Cross the village to the log tunnel on the west side, the one straight opposite the path you just came down.
steps.detail: It is the tunnel at ground level past the small bridges, not the Lost Woods tunnel up on the ledge behind the Know-It-All Brothers' house. Saria is not at her usual spot on the bridge railing; she is waiting further on.

steps.text: Walk through the log tunnel onto the long bridge that leaves the forest.
Keep walking along the bridge until Saria drops down in front of you and the goodbye scene starts.
steps.detail: You cannot avoid her and there is nothing to answer. Kokiri are not supposed to leave the forest, which is why she came to see you off.

steps.text: Accept the Fairy Ocarina from Saria at the end of the scene.
steps.detail: It is her parting gift and the instrument you will play every song on until you get the Ocarina of Time. Link runs off on his own once the scene finishes.

steps.text: Open the pause menu and put the Fairy Ocarina on a C button.
steps.detail: Item subscreen: highlight the ocarina, then press the C button you want it on. You have no songs yet, so playing it now only makes noise.

steps.text: Step off the end of the bridge into Hyrule Field and watch the flyover of the field.
steps.detail: The camera sweeps the whole field and settles on Hyrule Castle in the distance to the north. That castle is where this chapter is going.

steps.text: Walk forward and round the first corner of the path; Kaepora Gaebora, a huge owl, lands on the tree ahead of you.
steps.detail: You cannot walk past him. He is a recurring guide and will drop in like this several more times during the game.

steps.text: Talk through the owl's speech about Hyrule Castle and about the map you now carry.
steps.detail: The content is just a reminder that the castle to the north is your destination and that the map works out here in the field too.

steps.text: Answer his closing question with the option that does not send him back to the start of the speech.
steps.detail: He asks whether you want to hear it all again. The 'no' answer is usually the bottom line, but the game shuffles the order of the two options between encounters, so read both before pressing A.

steps.text: Run straight north up the road toward the castle and do not stop to explore; going directly gets you to the drawbridge before nightfall.
steps.detail: Lon Lon Ranch, Kakariko Village, Lake Hylia, Gerudo Valley and the Lost Woods are all reachable already, but their story objectives are still locked. Their Heart Pieces and Gold Skulltulas are collected in later chapters, so leave them.

steps.text: Pass the walled Lon Lon Ranch in the middle of the field and stay on the road to the moat at the north edge.
steps.detail: The ranch is the fenced circle with a ramp gate. Keep it to one side and keep running; the road curves up to the castle moat and the drawbridge.

steps.text: If the drawbridge is already raised for the night, stand on the road and wait there for sunrise.
steps.detail: Stalchildren claw their way out of the ground at night, but only if you step off the road onto the grass. Standing still on the road is safe, and the bridge lowers again at dawn.

steps.text: Cross the drawbridge and go up the entry passage into Hyrule Castle Town.
Come up the passage into the Market entrance, the small courtyard just inside the town gate.
Go through the first door on your right in this entrance courtyard, into the guardhouse.
steps.detail: The soldier inside is on duty to stop people wrecking the storeroom, but he is bored and lets you smash the lot.

steps.text: Smash the pots and the loose crates around the guardhouse with your sword and pick up the Rupees.
steps.detail: Roll into the crates or slash them; either breaks them. This is the best Rupee source you have access to right now.

steps.text: Break the crate in the back corner right beside the soldier; a Gold Skulltula jumps out of it.
steps.detail: It is one of the crates stacked behind him at the far end of the room, not the ones near the door.

steps.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula with one sword slash and pick up the token it drops.
steps.detail: It scuttles along the floor rather than clinging to a wall, so you can just walk up and hit it. Walk over the token to collect it.

steps.text: Farm the room: leave the guardhouse, walk straight back in to respawn the pots and crates, and smash them again until you hold at least 20 Rupees.
steps.detail: Re-entering resets the room every time, so repeat the loop as often as you need. The Shooting Gallery costs 20 Rupees; a child's wallet caps at 99.

steps.text: Leave the guardhouse, go back down the entry passage and out onto the drawbridge.
steps.detail: You are heading for three hidden Red Rupees on the bridge itself.

steps.text: Climb the chain on the left-hand side of the drawbridge all the way to the top.
steps.detail: Walk into the chain and Link grabs on, then climb with the stick. Go slowly; letting go drops you back to the bridge deck.

steps.text: From the top of that chain, jump off toward the middle of the bridge to grab a hidden Red Rupee worth 20.
steps.detail: Aim inward, over the bridge deck, not out toward the water. The Rupee is invisible until you touch it.

steps.text: Climb the chain on the other side of the drawbridge to the top the same way.
Jump toward the middle from that chain for the second hidden Red Rupee, 40 Rupees in total.
steps.detail: That is already more than the 20 the Shooting Gallery costs.

steps.text: For the third hidden Red Rupee, stand a little back from the wall on the chain, roll, and jump off from there.
steps.detail: This one sits in the centre of the bridge and only the rolling jump reaches it. It is fiddly; drop it after a few tries, the other 40 Rupees are enough.

steps.text: Walk back across the drawbridge and up into the Market square, the round plaza with the fountain.
Find the Shooting Gallery around the plaza: it is the shopfront with a bullseye sign hanging above its door.
steps.detail: Walk the ring of doors around the fountain until you see the bullseye. The Bazaar, the Happy Mask Shop and the Bombchu alley are the other doors here.

steps.text: Talk to the big-lipped owner inside and pay 20 Rupees for a round.
steps.detail: He hands you a round straight away once you agree and pay.

steps.text: Shoot all ten Rupee targets in one round with the Fairy Slingshot for a perfect score.
steps.detail: The targets pop up in exactly the same pattern every game, so a failed round is practice. Lead the moving ones: Deku Seeds take a moment to reach them. If you only miss one or two he lets you play again free, so keep going until the round is perfect.

steps.text: Take the bigger Bullet Bag that the perfect round earns; it holds 40 Deku Seeds.
steps.detail: Only the very first perfect round gives the bag. Perfect rounds after that pay 50 Rupees instead, which is still a decent earner.

steps.text: Step back out of the Shooting Gallery into the Market square.
Leave the Market square by the road on the north side and follow it up out of town to the Hyrule Castle grounds.
steps.detail: It is the archway opposite the way you came in from the drawbridge. The road climbs past the Temple of Time turning and ends at the castle gate area.

steps.text: Walk forward onto the castle grounds path; Kaepora Gaebora drops in front of you a second time.
Talk through the owl's speech about how time passes.
steps.detail: The useful part: time stands still inside the town and inside houses, but keeps moving out here and in Hyrule Field. Whenever you need day or night to change, wait out here, never in the Market.

steps.text: Roll into the lone tree standing to the left of the path near the entrance; a Gold Skulltula falls out of it.
steps.detail: Press A while running to roll, and hit the trunk square on. Nothing happens if you only walk into it.

steps.text: Slash the Gold Skulltula that landed at the foot of the tree and take its token.
steps.detail: One hit kills it on the ground. Step over the token to pick it up.

steps.text: Walk back down the road into the Market square.
steps.detail: This trip is what moves Malon. The red-haired girl who was standing in the Market goes up to the castle grounds once you have been up there and come back. If she was already at the vines on your first visit, skip this and the next step.

steps.text: Turn around and take the road back up to the castle grounds.
Walk over to the ivy-covered cliff to the left of the first guarded gate; Malon is standing at the bottom of it.
Talk to Malon and hear her out about her father.
steps.detail: She is from Lon Lon Ranch in the middle of Hyrule Field. Her father Talon came up to the castle to deliver crates of Lon Lon Milk and never came home; she is sure he has fallen asleep somewhere inside.

steps.text: Take the Weird Egg she gives you so you can wake Talon when you find him.
Put the Weird Egg on a C button in the pause menu.
steps.detail: It hatches into a Cucco at the next dawn, and only while time is running, so it will not hatch while you stand in town.

steps.text: Climb the vines on the cliff next to Malon to the top.
steps.detail: The gate beside her is guarded and the guard will not let you through; the cliff is the way in.

steps.text: Walk along the top of the cliff away from the gate, to the far end of the ledge.
steps.detail: Do not head toward the guard. Getting caught anywhere on the grounds dumps you back at the entrance and you restart the sneak from these vines.

steps.text: Drop off the end of the ledge and land on the far side of the gate.
Turn to face the castle and read the guards: two patrol the bright road up to the right, one stands higher up on the left.
Climb the grass slope straight up the gap between that pair on the right and the single guard on the left.
steps.detail: A guard only notices what is in front of him, so the gap between two patrols is safe as long as you keep moving and do not cut across anyone's face.

steps.text: At the top of the slope, get off the bright gravel road and stay on the grass to the left.
steps.detail: The road is where the patrols walk. The grass strip to its left runs parallel and is out of their view.

steps.text: Follow the grass forward on the left until a second gate with a guard on each side comes into view.
Go to the stones that stick out of the cliff face just to the left of that gate.
steps.detail: On the N64 version they are pale stones jutting from the rock; other versions draw vines there instead. Either way, walk into them and Link grabs on.

steps.text: Climb the stones to the top of the cliff.
Walk over the top and drop down on the other side of the gate, behind the two guards.
Ahead is a third gate with two more guards; instead of walking up to it, jump into the moat on the right.
steps.detail: There is no way past this gate on foot. The moat runs along the wall and around the guards.

steps.text: Swim along the moat, following the castle wall past the gate toward the far corner.
steps.detail: Link swims by himself once he is in; just steer. Watch the air meter and surface if it runs low, but the swim is short.

steps.text: Grab the Rupees floating in the moat as you swim past them.
steps.detail: They sit right along the route, so it costs nothing to pick them up on the way.

steps.text: Climb out of the moat at the far corner.
Follow the grass along the castle wall until you find Talon, fast asleep beside his crates of Lon Lon Milk.
If the Weird Egg has not hatched yet, stand here on the grounds and wait for dawn.
steps.detail: Time only moves outdoors, and here counts as outdoors, so waiting next to Talon works. The egg hatches into a Cucco at sunrise.

steps.text: Put the hatched Cucco on a C button in the pause menu.
Stand right next to Talon and use the Cucco; its crowing wakes him.
steps.detail: Get close enough that Link is almost touching him or the noise will not reach.

steps.text: Talk to Talon through his dialogue until he panics and runs off home.
steps.detail: He confirms Malon's story about the milk delivery and the nap, then bolts the moment he hears his daughter sent you after him. He leaves the crates behind, which is what you actually need.

steps.text: Grab the first milk crate with A and push it into the moat water against the wall.
steps.detail: Line yourself up square against a face of the crate before grabbing, then push it in. It floats and stays put.

steps.text: Push the second crate into the water so it snaps into place on top of the first.
steps.detail: It will only stack if you push it in beside the first one; the game clicks it into position.

steps.text: Climb onto the stack of crates.
Jump from the top crate across to the ledge where water pours out of the castle wall.
Check that it is daytime before you go any further; if night has fallen, drop back down and wait on the grounds for sunrise.
steps.detail: Two guards stand behind the hole at night and grab you the second you come through, throwing you back outside the grounds.

steps.text: Crawl through the small hole beside the waterspout into the castle courtyard.
Stand up out of the crawlspace and stay still for a moment to watch the first guard walk his loop.
steps.detail: The courtyard is a chain of small gardens, each with a guard walking a fixed circuit around the hedges, flower beds and statues. A guard sees only what is in front of him: behind him is safe, either side is not. Being spotted throws you all the way back outside the grounds, and you redo the whole sneak from Malon's vines.

steps.text: The moment the first guard turns away, walk up behind him and past along the hedge.
Slip past the next guard by keeping the flower bed between the two of you.
steps.detail: Move while he is on the far side of it, and stop when he swings back around toward your side.

steps.text: Move into the next stretch of the courtyard as soon as the guard there starts walking away from you.
Use the fountain in the middle of that stretch to stay out of the next guard's sight while he circles it.
steps.detail: Circle the fountain the same way he does, staying opposite him, until you are past.

steps.text: Cross behind the last guard and reach the far end of the courtyard.
steps.detail: This is the last one; after him nothing patrols.

steps.text: Turn left at the far end into the quiet part of the gardens.
steps.detail: No guards at all in here, so you can stop creeping.

steps.text: Shoot the window on the right-hand wall with the Fairy Slingshot for a Red Rupee.
steps.detail: The picture in that window is a cameo of Mario, Luigi, Yoshi, Peach and Bowser. Do not shoot the window on the left: a guard leans out of it and throws a Bomb at you.

steps.text: Walk up to Princess Zelda at the window at the back of the garden and talk to her.
steps.detail: She is peering through the glass into the throne room and does not notice you until you speak.

steps.text: Sit through her account of the Triforce and of the dream that foretold you.
steps.detail: Whoever touches the Triforce in the Sacred Realm is granted their wish, which is why the way in is sealed behind the three Spiritual Stones and the Ocarina of Time.

steps.text: Look through the window when she asks you to, and see Ganondorf kneeling before the King.
steps.detail: He notices you looking. This is the Gerudo man from her dream and the reason she is in a hurry.

steps.text: Agree to fetch the two remaining Spiritual Stones before Ganondorf can reach the Sacred Realm.
steps.detail: You already hold the Kokiri's Emerald from the Great Deku Tree; the Goron's Ruby and the Zora's Sapphire are still out there.

steps.text: Take Zelda's Letter from her at the end of the conversation.
steps.detail: It carries her royal seal and proves you act on her authority. You will need to show it to the guard blocking the Death Mountain gate in Kakariko Village.

steps.text: Walk back toward the garden exit; Impa, Zelda's attendant, steps in front of you.
Listen to Impa and let her teach you Zelda's Lullaby.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Left, C-Up, C-Right, C-Left, C-Up, C-Right. Link plays it through by himself during the scene and it is added to your song list. It opens anything marked with the royal family's crest.

steps.text: Let Impa lead you out of the castle and point out Kakariko Village at the foot of Death Mountain.
steps.detail: The cutscene carries you all the way out and leaves you on the road outside Castle Town in Hyrule Field. Death Mountain is next in the story, but the following chapter clears several side areas first.

steps.text: Cross Hyrule Field to the north-east and climb the long stone stairway into Kakariko Village.
steps.detail: Impa told you to come here. It is also the way up to Death Mountain for the next chapter, so the trip is never wasted.

steps.text: Walk across the village to the far right side and take the exit at the top of the steps into the Graveyard.
steps.detail: Almost nothing in this chapter is needed to finish the game: it is Heart Pieces, Gold Skulltulas, bottles and capacity upgrades. Skip straight to Dodongo's Cavern if you only want the main quest.

steps.text: At the very back of the Graveyard, read the left and the right grave of the three large ones to summon the ghosts of the Composer Brothers.
steps.detail: Press A facing each headstone. Sharp and Flat wrote a song that moves the sun; they only talk, there is nothing to fight.

steps.text: Stand on the Triforce tile in front of the big middle grave and play Zelda's Lullaby.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Left, C-Up, C-Right, C-Left, C-Up, C-Right. A storm rolls in and lightning blows the tombstone apart.

steps.text: Drop into the hole the lightning opened, into the Royal Family's Tomb.
Walk down the ramp and kill all five Keese with the Fairy Slingshot to open the door at the far end.
steps.detail: Keese are bats. The door stays shut until every one of the five is dead; shoot them as they swoop in.

steps.text: Climb the huge steps and go through the door that opened.
Cross the next room along the stone ledges to the door on the far side, keeping away from the two ReDeads and out of the green pools.
steps.detail: ReDeads freeze you with a scream, then grab on and drain hearts, and they are only safe to kill from behind. The green sludge hurts too. Hug the edges and keep moving; you do not have to fight anything here.

steps.text: Press A at the big stone tablet in the last passage; Navi reads the inscription and you learn the Sun's Song.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Right, C-Down, C-Up, C-Right, C-Down, C-Up. Outdoors it flips day to night and night to day instantly, and it freezes ReDeads and Gibdos solid. The rest of this chapter leans on it constantly.

steps.text: Head back out through the ReDead room, playing the Sun's Song to freeze any ReDead that comes at you.
Step on the coloured pad in the first room to warp back up to the Graveyard.
Stand between the back row of graves and the Royal Family's Tomb facing the entrance, then pull back the fourth grave from the left and drop into the hole.
steps.detail: Grab the headstone with A and walk backwards to drag it clear of the hole.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to freeze the ReDead down here, walk around behind it and slash it until it dies.
steps.detail: Frozen, it cannot grab you. Get fully behind it before swinging; hits from the front barely hurt it, and if it grabs you it drains hearts fast.

steps.text: Stand on the steps of the raised platform and play the Sun's Song again to make a large chest appear.
Open the chest for a Piece of Heart.
Warp out on the coloured pad, then go to the front row of graves near the entrance, pull back the one with three flowers in front of it and drop in.
Open the small chest for a free Hylian Shield.
steps.detail: The Bazaar in Castle Town sells one, so this chest just saves you the Rupees. Take it anyway: adult Link cannot use a Deku Shield at all, and the next dungeon is easier with it.

steps.text: Step on the coloured pad to leave the grave.
Play the Sun's Song if it is still daytime, then find Dampe the gravekeeper walking around the Graveyard.
steps.detail: His Heart-Pounding Gravedigging Tour only runs between 18:00 and 21:00. Straight after learning the Sun's Song you are already inside that window. The guard at the Kakariko entrance tells you the current time.

steps.text: Talk to Dampe and pay 10 Rupees to start the Heart-Pounding Gravedigging Tour.
Lead Dampe onto one of the soft soil spots and stand still so he digs there.
steps.detail: He follows you and digs wherever you stop. The prize in each hole is random: usually Rupees, sometimes nothing, and roughly one dig in ten is a Piece of Heart.

steps.text: Pick up whatever he throws out, pay another 10 Rupees and dig a different spot; keep repeating.
steps.detail: The Piece of Heart is guaranteed inside the first 15 holes he digs, and he uncovers enough Rupees that the game roughly pays for itself. If your wallet runs dry, leave it and come back later in the game; nothing is lost.

steps.text: The moment a dig throws out a Piece of Heart, run over and pick it up off the ground.
steps.missable: Pick up Dampe's dug-up Piece of Heart before the tour ends or you leave the Graveyard, or it is gone for this playthrough.
steps.detail: WARNING: a dug-up Piece of Heart must be collected before the tour ends or before you leave the area. Walk away from it and the game still counts it as taken, and it never appears in another hole again.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to bring back daytime, then walk down out of the Graveyard into Kakariko Village.
steps.detail: Anju the Cucco Lady only stands out by her pen during the day.

steps.text: Talk to Anju, the woman waving her arms in front of the small fenced pen near the Graveyard steps, to start the Cucco round-up.
steps.detail: Seven Cuccos are loose in the village and she pays out once all seven are inside the fence. Do not hit them: strike one too often and a flock swarms you until you leave the area or die.

steps.text: Cucco 1: pick up the one wandering between Anju's pen and the Graveyard steps and drop it inside the fence.
Cucco 2: knock the one on the ledge beside the House of Skulltula down with a Slingshot shot or a Deku Nut, then chase it and carry it to the pen.
steps.detail: You can also carry another Cucco up onto the unfinished building in the construction area and glide across to it.

steps.text: Cucco 3: grab the one by the village entrance gate and carry it to the pen.
Cucco 4: roll into the crate beside the stairs up to the higher part of the village, then carry the Cucco that pops out to the pen.
Cucco 5: pick up the one loitering by the ramp in front of the guard at the Death Mountain gate and take it down to the pen.
Pick up a spare Cucco and climb onto the platform by the windmill door.
steps.detail: The last two birds are in a walled-off corner in the north-east that has no normal way in. This is the setup for getting over the fence.

steps.text: Holding the Cucco, jump off that ledge at an angle so you glide onto the narrow fence on the left nearest the Potion Shop, then drop into the walled-off corner of the village.
steps.detail: Alternative: climb the lookout tower, hold Z facing the middle of the village and side-jump left onto the fence top. If you miss, pick the Cucco back up and try again; there is no penalty.

steps.text: Cucco 6: in the lower part of the walled corner, next to the open hole, pick up the Cucco and throw it over the fence.
steps.detail: Do not walk into the hole. Throw the bird well clear of the fence so you can find it again from outside.

steps.text: Cucco 7: climb the ladder in the walled corner and grab the Cucco waiting at the top.
Jump down holding that Cucco to glide back over the fence, then carry both loose birds into the pen.
With all seven Cuccos in the pen, talk to Anju for an Empty Bottle.
steps.detail: She explains she is allergic to her own chickens. Put the bottle on a C button: the next steps need it to carry bugs.

steps.text: Go back up to the Graveyard, lift the lone rock in the patch of bushes by the entrance and immediately swipe the Empty Bottle at one of the bugs underneath.
steps.detail: The bugs burrow away within a couple of seconds, so put the bottle on a C button before you lift the rock.

steps.text: Carry the bugs to the patch of soft soil on the left of the Graveyard, by the five graves standing on their own, and empty the bottle onto it.
Kill the Gold Skulltula that bursts out of the soil and take its token.
steps.detail: Hit its soft back, or just slash it as it turns. If the token floats out of reach, jump-attack while Z-targeted to grab it.

steps.text: Walk back down into Kakariko Village and play the Sun's Song to bring on night, when the Gold Skulltulas come out.
steps.detail: Five of them are in the village, all outdoors. They rattle loudly, so turn the sound up if you lose one.

steps.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula on one of the bare wall frames of the unfinished building in the construction area and take the token.
Kill the Gold Skulltula clinging to the outside wall of the House of Skulltula and take the token.
Roll into the big tree in the middle of the village to shake a Gold Skulltula loose, kill it and take the token.
steps.detail: Back off right after the roll so it does not drop on your head.

steps.text: Shoot the Gold Skulltula on the ladder of the lookout tower with the Slingshot, then climb the ladder to reach the token.
Kill the Gold Skulltula on the side of the house nearest the Death Mountain gate and take the token.
Go into the House of Skulltula, the building across from the construction area.
Talk to the cursed spider man in the middle of the room.
steps.detail: His family is under the Curse of the Spider. One member is freed at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 100 tokens, and each one hands over a reward. Everything past 50 is only for a full clear.

steps.text: Talk to the freed family member doing jumping jacks on the right for the Adult's Wallet.
steps.detail: You are on 11 tokens, past the 10 needed. The Adult's Wallet holds 200 Rupees instead of 99.

steps.text: Leave Kakariko Village for Hyrule Field and head for Lon Lon Ranch, the walled ranch in the middle of the map.
steps.detail: You cannot miss it on the minimap. The way in is a ramp through the wall.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song if it is night so that it is daytime inside the ranch.
steps.detail: Talon only runs his game by day, and Malon only stands out in the corral by day.

steps.text: Just inside the ranch, go through the door on your left into the house where Talon is standing.
Before talking to him, pick up every ordinary Cucco in the room and throw it into the corner at the foot of the stairs.
steps.detail: Clearing the decoys out first turns the mini-game into a walkover: only the three Super Cuccos are left loose in the room.

steps.text: Talk to Talon and pay 10 Rupees to play Super Cuccos.
steps.detail: He shoos three special Cuccos into the corners of the room and puts you on a short timer.

steps.text: Pick up all three Super Cuccos before the time runs out, working one corner at a time.
steps.detail: Throw any wrong bird well away so you do not grab it twice. If you lose, just pay and play again.

steps.text: Talk to Talon after winning to receive a bottle of Lon Lon Milk.
steps.detail: The bottle is the prize; the milk inside is two drinks worth five hearts each. He also starts hinting about marrying his daughter. Put it on a C button.

steps.text: Leave the house and round the corner on the left to a tree standing on its own.
Roll into the lone tree, kill the Gold Skulltula that drops out and take the token.
Walk into the middle of the corral and talk to Malon.
steps.detail: She chats about the castle and her father, then introduces Epona, who immediately bolts away from you.

steps.text: Keep talking to Malon until she brings up the song her mother wrote, then take out the Ocarina standing in front of her to learn Epona's Song.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Up, C-Left, C-Right, C-Up, C-Left, C-Right. Later chapters need it to call Epona as an adult, and it draws free milk out of any cow.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to bring on night.
Follow the outside of the corral clockwise to the wooden feeding trough in its south-east corner and kill the Gold Skulltula on the boards, then take the token.
steps.detail: Guays, the black crows, dive at you out here. This spider is only on the trough at night.

steps.text: Go into the tall feed silo in the south-west corner of the ranch.
Pull the front crates out of the way with A and climb up onto the stack.
Work across and down to the far corner behind the crates, where a small crawl hole sits at floor level.
steps.detail: Push, pull and climb until the corner opens up; there is no trick to it beyond shuffling the boxes.

steps.text: Crawl through the hole and take the Piece of Heart inside.
Leave Lon Lon Ranch and head due west across Hyrule Field to the path into Gerudo Valley.
steps.detail: The valley entrance is straight west of the ranch, at the far edge of the field.

steps.text: Just inside the valley, lift the three rocks on your right and catch the bugs under one of them in the empty bottle.
steps.detail: Put the bottle on a C button before you lift, or the bugs burrow away first.

steps.text: Walk forward and pick up the Cucco near the bridge.
Carrying the Cucco, jump off the right-hand side of the bridge and glide down to the ledge on the left at the bottom of the valley.
steps.detail: Hold the stick to steer as you fall and look down to line up the landing. Falling in the river is not a disaster: the current is slow here and you can swim back and climb out.

steps.text: Find the patch of soft soil near the Gerudo woman and her cow on the valley floor and empty the bugs onto it.
Kill the Gold Skulltula that pops out of the soil and take the token.
Walk to the waterfall at the end of the valley floor and drop into the water behind it.
Climb the ladder in the alcove behind the waterfall.
Take the Piece of Heart at the top of the ladder.
Jump into the river, let the current carry you down into Lake Hylia, then swim ashore and leave by the north exit into Hyrule Field.
steps.detail: There is no climb back up the valley from the bottom; the river is the only way out, and it always ends in Lake Hylia.

steps.text: Cross Hyrule Field back to the Gerudo Valley path and walk up to the bridge again.
Pick up the Cucco by the bridge and this time glide off the LEFT side, aiming for the small platform with a single crate on it.
steps.detail: The platform is across the gap, clearly visible from the bridge. Steer the whole way down; the Cucco gives you plenty of float.

steps.text: Roll into the crate on the platform for a Piece of Heart.
Jump into the river again and ride the current down to Lake Hylia.
Go to the little fenced plot on the north-east side of the lake and talk to Bonooru, the lower of the two scarecrows.
steps.detail: The upper one is Pierre. Bonooru boasts that he never forgets a tune.

steps.text: Take out the Ocarina in front of Bonooru and play eight notes of your own invention; he memorises them as the Scarecrow's Song.
steps.detail: WRITE THE EIGHT NOTES DOWN. As an adult you must play the exact same eight to summon Pierre at Hookshot spots, and a couple of Heart Pieces depend on him. Avoid anything that matches a real song.

steps.text: Slash the lone bush on the ledge above, beside Pierre, and bottle the bugs it hides.
Cross to the Lakeside Laboratory, the big house with the chimney on the far side of the lake, and empty the bugs onto the soft soil beside it.
Kill the Gold Skulltula that comes out of the soil and take the token.
Swim out to the smaller island with two stone pillars, in the south-east corner of the lake.
Play the Sun's Song to bring on night.
Kill the Gold Skulltula that appears on the island and take the token.
steps.detail: It only shows up at night; by day the island is empty.

steps.text: Swim over to the Fishing Pond on the east shore and go inside.
Pay the owner 20 Rupees to rent a rod.
steps.detail: A casts and reels, B wiggles the lure, the stick steers the line. Above all, do not scare the fish: once spooked they all run for deep water.

steps.text: Stand on the arched log near the three sticks poking out of the water and cast at the biggest fish.
steps.detail: The largest fish always starts by the arched log. Fishing from on top of the log means far less line to reel in. Let the lure drift close, then wiggle with B to attract it.

steps.text: Once it bites, hold the stick back and hold A to haul it in without letting go.
steps.detail: Hold both, do not tap. If it still gets away, walk out of the pond and come back in: every fish resets to its starting spot.

steps.text: Show the owner a fish weighing 10 pounds or more to beat the pond record and get a Piece of Heart.
Cross Hyrule Field to the forest entrance on the east side and follow the tunnel into Kokiri Forest.
steps.detail: Leave Lake Hylia by its north exit first. A Peahat may lift off near the road on the way; you are never required to fight one, so just run past.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to bring on night.
Go up to the fenced training area in the south-west of the village, walk around the back of the Know-It-All Brothers' House and kill the Gold Skulltula on the rear wall, then take the token.
steps.detail: Only there at night. Jump-attack while Z-targeted if the token hangs too high to touch.

steps.text: From the village entrance, head left and climb the small ledge behind Mido's House.
Climb the vines on the wall above that ledge.
Follow the path along the top round to the hollow log and go through it into the Lost Woods.
Take the right-hand passage out of the entrance room into a wide clearing with a single tree ahead.
steps.detail: This is also the first turn of the route to the Sacred Forest Meadow. A wrong exit anywhere in the Lost Woods spits you back out, so follow the exits exactly as written.

steps.text: Shoot the target hanging from the lone branch with the Slingshot and hit the middle three times in a row.
steps.detail: A dead-centre hit is worth 100 points; anything less resets the run. Just keep shooting, there is no cost.

steps.text: Shoot the hanging target on the lone tree branch and hit the centre three times in a row; a Deku Scrub appears and upgrades your Bullet Bag again.
steps.detail: Each bullseye scores 100. This is the second Bullet Bag upgrade of the run, after the one from the Market Shooting Gallery. Sources disagree on which gallery gives 40 and which gives 50, so flag this step if the capacity you get is not the higher one.

steps.text: Drop down into the lower part of the clearing and stand on the tree stump on the right; two Skull Kids appear on the stumps nearby.
Take out the Ocarina to join in, then copy each tune back note for note as they add one note per round.
steps.detail: It is Simon with an Ocarina. Writing the notes down on paper as they play makes it much easier.

steps.text: Finish three tunes in a row without a mistake for a Piece of Heart.
Take the left exit.
steps.detail: If you lose the thread, follow the music: the correct exit is the one Saria's melody gets louder toward. Kaepora Gaebora drops in around here to tell you the same thing.

steps.text: Take the right exit.
Take the left exit.
Go straight ahead.
Take the left exit.
Take the right exit into the Sacred Forest Meadow.
steps.detail: The whole route from the Lost Woods entrance, for reference: right, left, right, left, forward, left, right.

steps.text: Walk forward into the hedge maze; a Wolfos claws its way out of the ground and bars seal the way on.
Kill the Wolfos to make the bars ahead vanish.
steps.detail: Z-target and keep the shield up while you close in, then strike right after it swings or when it turns its back. Two or three sword hits finish it.

steps.text: Round the next corner and deal with the Mad Scrub.
steps.detail: Mad Scrubs spit three seeds at a time. Z-target, walk in behind a raised shield and slash, or stun it with a Deku Nut, or pick it off from range with the Slingshot.

steps.text: Work north through the hedge maze using the minimap, killing or running past the Mad Scrubs in the side passages.
steps.detail: Several branches are dead ends; the minimap shows which corridors actually connect. Nothing here is required, so running is fine.

steps.text: At the far side, take the stone steps rather than the ladder beside them.
Kill the two Mad Scrubs guarding the huge archway at the top of the steps.
steps.detail: Deal with them one at a time so you are not caught in crossfire from both.

steps.text: Walk up the last ramp to the altar at the top of the meadow.
Watch the scene with Saria and learn Saria's Song.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left. This one is not optional: you must play it for Darunia in Goron City to get the Goron's Bracelet.

steps.text: Climb the ladder at the foot of the temple ramp onto the tops of the hedge walls, then take the ladder in the middle down into the Fairy Fountain to heal up.
steps.detail: Walking the hedge tops skips every Mad Scrub on the way out. Leave a bottle empty rather than catching a fairy: the Lost Woods steps below need one free for bugs.

steps.text: Hop along the hedge tops back to the meadow entrance and leave into the Lost Woods.
Sit through Kaepora Gaebora's speech when he drops in.
steps.detail: His one useful line: wherever a musical staff appears over your head with the Ocarina out, a song is meant to be played there.

steps.text: Take a wrong exit on purpose so the Lost Woods throw you back out into Kokiri Forest.
Go back through the log into the Lost Woods and take the LEFT passage this time, to the clearing with a single Skull Kid playing a flute.
steps.detail: Walk straight at him and he runs off. Head for the tree stump instead and he stands watching you.

steps.text: Stand on the tree stump, take out the Ocarina and play Saria's Song for the Skull Kid to get a Piece of Heart.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left. Any other song just makes him happy; only Saria's Song pays out.

steps.text: Take the left exit again and drop all the way down into the lowest part of the area below the bridge.
Z-target the Business Scrub on the far side and reflect its nut back with your shield to knock it over.
steps.detail: Hold the shield up facing it; the nut bounces off and floors it. Then talk to it instead of finishing it off.

steps.text: Pay the Business Scrub 40 Rupees to carry 20 Deku Sticks instead of 10.
steps.detail: One of the two Deku Stick capacity upgrades in the game; the order you collect them in does not matter.

steps.text: Find bugs down here, under a rock or in the grass, and catch them in the empty bottle.
steps.detail: Bugs are all over the Lost Woods, so topping the bottle back up is never a problem.

steps.text: Empty the bugs onto the patch of soft soil in this same area below the bridge.
Kill the Gold Skulltula that pops out and take the token.
Catch another bottle of bugs here before moving on.
Go back to the Lost Woods entrance room and take the right passage.
Take the left exit, then the right exit.
Take the left exit, then the left exit again, into a meadow clearing.
steps.detail: The full route from the entrance is right, left, right, left, left. Only that last turn differs from the Sacred Forest Meadow route, where you go forward instead.

steps.text: Walk forward to the patch of soft soil in the meadow and empty the bugs onto it.
Kill the Gold Skulltula that comes out and take the token.
Catch one last bottle of bugs in this clearing.
Take a wrong exit on purpose to get dumped back in Kokiri Forest.
Go to the Kokiri Shop where you bought the Deku Shield and empty the bugs onto the patch of soft soil directly behind it.
Kill the Gold Skulltula that pops out and take the token.
steps.detail: That makes 20 tokens, which frees another member of the family in the House of Skulltula.

steps.text: Leave Kokiri Forest for Hyrule Field and go north to Hyrule Castle Town, crossing the drawbridge while it is still daylight.
steps.detail: The drawbridge is raised at night, so you have to be inside before dark and change the time from in there.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song inside the Market to turn it to night.
steps.detail: Time does not pass by itself in the Market, so the song is the only way to flip it. Dogs now run loose in the square; touching the wrong one makes it trail you until you leave the area.

steps.text: Go to the blue vendor stand near the Bazaar and touch the white puppy, Richard, so he follows you.
steps.detail: The stand is under the window with the man leaning out of it. Richard is the small white dog; the others are no use.

steps.text: Lead Richard to the right-hand side of the square and out through either exit into the Back Alley.
steps.detail: Glance back now and then to check he is still with you. If he wandered off, walk back and touch him again.

steps.text: In the Back Alley, go to the left side and take Richard through the one door that is only open at night.
Talk to the woman in the blue dress inside; she recognises Richard and hands over a Piece of Heart.
Leave Castle Town and cross Hyrule Field back to Kakariko Village.
Go into the House of Skulltula.
Talk to the newly freed family member for the Stone of Agony.
steps.detail: The 20-token reward. It chimes whenever you are near a hidden secret, and rumbles the controller on N64 if a Rumble Pak is in. It only really earns its keep once you have Bombs.

steps.text: In Kakariko Village, lift the small rock just inside the Graveyard entrance and catch the bugs underneath in an empty bottle.
steps.detail: You need them for a soft soil patch outside Dodongo's Cavern; there are no bugs up on the mountain. Scoop them with the bottle as soon as they scurry out.

steps.text: Climb to the top of Kakariko Village and show Zelda's Letter to the guard at the Death Mountain gate. He opens it for you.
steps.detail: Sit through his speech; the mask he mentions is a later side quest. Equip the Hylian Shield before going up. If you never took the free one from the Graveyard, the Bazaar in the Market now sells it for 60 Rupees.

steps.text: Head up Death Mountain Trail past the Red Tektites and talk to the Goron standing next to the huge boulder that seals Dodongo's Cavern.
steps.detail: Z-target a Tektite, wait for it to jump at you and press B without moving the stick to slash it out of the air. Deku Nuts also stun them. The Goron explains Ganondorf sealed the cavern.

steps.text: Continue up the trail into the wide area with the flag, keep clear of the rolling Goron, and enter the bannered doorway of Goron City.
steps.detail: The rolling Goron circles near the flag; if he hits you, you get knocked off the ledge and have to climb back up.

steps.text: Drop down tier by tier to the bottom floor of Goron City and stand on the carpet in front of the big closed door.
steps.detail: Jumping straight down from the entrance tier is the fastest way. The Goron by the door hints at the solution.

steps.text: Play Zelda's Lullaby on the carpet to open Darunia's door.
Light a Deku Stick on a torch inside Darunia's chamber and light every unlit torch around the bottom floor until the giant urn in the center of the city starts spinning.
steps.detail: The stick burns out after a while; light a fresh one at the chamber torches if needed. The spinning urn is used for a Piece of Heart shortly.

steps.text: With a lit Deku Stick, follow the right wall from Darunia's door up the steps to the corridor blocked by boulders and touch a Bomb Flower beside them to blast open the Lost Woods shortcut.
steps.detail: The Bomb Flowers on either side of the boulders ignite from the flame of your stick. Step back after lighting one; the chain of explosions clears the tunnel. Not required, but it saves a lot of walking later.

steps.text: Stand in front of Darunia and play Saria's Song. After his dance he gives you the Goron's Bracelet.
steps.detail: The bracelet lets you pick up Bomb Flowers, which you need to open Dodongo's Cavern. If you never learned Saria's Song, take the new shortcut into the Lost Woods (left, left, forward, left, right to the Sacred Forest Meadow), learn it from Saria at the far end, and come back (left, right, forward, right, right).

steps.text: Climb to the second tier from the bottom, turn left, grab the Bomb Flower at the top of the next steps and throw it into the spinning urn so it explodes while the smiling face is toward you; a Piece of Heart pops out.
steps.detail: The urn must still be spinning (relight the bottom-floor torches if it stopped). The timing takes a few tries; the Bomb Flower regrows, so keep throwing. The heart piece appears at the base of the urn.

steps.text: Leave Goron City through the top exit, back onto Death Mountain Trail.
From the Goron City entrance, go right along the ledge to the overhang where a lone Goron sits next to a Bomb Flower.
Pick up the Bomb Flower and throw it straight over the ledge so it lands beside the boulder below, blowing open the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern.
steps.detail: Aim straight ahead from the edge. If it misses, wait for the Bomb Flower to regrow and try again. Then walk back down to the trail.

steps.text: Drop your bottled bugs on the soft soil patch just outside Dodongo's Cavern, kill the Gold Skulltula that crawls out and grab its token.
steps.detail: The soft soil is the round dirt patch next to the cavern entrance. If you have no bugs, get them from under the rock by the Graveyard entrance in Kakariko Village.

steps.text: Enter Dodongo's Cavern, pick up one of the Bomb Flowers by the entrance and blow up the cracked wall straight ahead to open the main cavern. Equip the Hylian Shield.
steps.detail: Fire enemies burn the Deku Shield; keep the Hylian Shield on for the whole dungeon.

steps.text: In the main room, reach the raised area on the left side, use its lone Bomb Flower on the cracked wall there and open the big chest for the Dungeon Map.
steps.detail: Either hop onto the middle platform (stay out of the Beamos statue's gaze) and then left, or follow the strip of dry ground along the lava at the left edge, round the back and climb the ladder. The other cracked wall here only hides a Business Scrub selling Deku Shields.

steps.text: Cross to the raised area on the right side of the main room, pick up its Bomb Flower and throw it at the Beamos on that platform to destroy it.
steps.detail: The first cracked wall on this side only hides a Gossip Stone, which you cannot use yet. The Bomb Flower regrows after each throw.

steps.text: Use the regrown Bomb Flower to blow open the cracked wall behind where the Beamos stood, and go through the passage.
Fight through the Baby Dodongos in the winding corridor and climb the ledge at the end to reach the barred door with a floor switch.
steps.detail: Slash a Baby Dodongo as it nears you, then step away: it explodes after dying. Halfway along, a cracked wall on the right hides a Gold Skulltula; you come back for it once you have Bombs.

steps.text: Push or pull one of the two Armos statues onto the floor switch to hold the barred door open, then go through.
steps.detail: These statues are inert. Grab one from the side facing the switch and push it straight on.

steps.text: Pass the short corridor with two Keese and enter the next room.
In the lower Lizalfos room, defeat both Lizalfos to unlock the doors, then continue through the far door.
steps.detail: They attack one at a time. Z-target the active one, keep your shield up and slash between its attacks; when it jumps over you, just hold the shield. Stay off the lava. The pots by the door hold hearts.

steps.text: In the long Dodongo room, kill the three Dodongos by hitting their tails.
steps.detail: Stand in front of one until it starts its fire breath, circle behind and hit its tail, then back off before it spins. Slingshot shots between attacks also work. The cracked wall in the corner near the entrance only hides a Business Scrub selling Deku Sticks.

steps.text: Light a Deku Stick on the one lit torch in the Dodongo room and light the three unlit torches to open the barred door, then go through.
steps.detail: Grab the flame near the start of the room and light the torches on the way to the far door.

steps.text: Back in the main room on an upper ledge, step on the floor switch to open the barred door across the room, then drop down and cross to it.
steps.detail: The opened door is on the lower level on the far side; go around the lava the way you came.

steps.text: In the giant staircase room, use one of the Bomb Flowers to blow open the cracked wall on the left, revealing a door, and go through.
In the Compass room, wake and defeat the Armos, then open the big chest for the Compass.
steps.detail: Touch the statue to wake it and back off. Stun it with a Deku Nut and jump-attack it; it explodes when it dies, so hold the Hylian Shield up or run. Return to the staircase room afterward.

steps.text: Pick up the lone Bomb Flower near the Compass room door and set it in the gap in the row of Bomb Flowers along the big pillar; the chain explosion sinks the pillar into a giant staircase.
steps.detail: Stand well back once it is placed.

steps.text: Climb the giant stairs and walk around to the vines on the south wall; shoot the Skullwalltulas and the Gold Skulltula there with the Slingshot, then climb up for the token.
steps.detail: The Gold Skulltula sits on the vines at the back (south) of the room. Kill it from below with the Slingshot before climbing so it cannot knock you off.

steps.text: Go through the door at the top of the staircase room into the hexagonal Armos room and shoot the Fire Keese with the Slingshot.
steps.detail: Fire Keese set a Deku Shield alight; keep the Hylian Shield equipped.

steps.text: Find the side of the central platform with the ladder, pull the inert Armos statue away from it, climb up and step on the switch to open the doors. Drop down and take the door the switch points you toward.
steps.detail: The living Armos statues do not need to be touched; only the one blocking the ladder moves.

steps.text: Back in the main room on the second floor above the entrance, cross the bridge to the far side, jumping the gap in the middle, and enter the next room.
steps.detail: Two Fire Keese patrol here; shoot them before jumping the gap so they cannot knock you off.

steps.text: In the Blade Trap room, jump straight down between the two pillars and go straight ahead, watching for the sliding traps, until you reach the stone block.
steps.detail: Blade Traps rush along fixed lines and return; wait for one to slide back before crossing its path. Use Z-targeting to peek around corners. A Recovery Heart sits in the hole behind the block.

steps.text: Pull the stone block over to the platform, climb up and open the small chest for a Red Rupee.
Pick up the Bomb Flower on the platform and throw it at the cracked wall above the ladder, then jump over and continue.
steps.detail: The Bomb Flower regrows if you miss. If landing it on the small ledge is hard, hold it until it flashes quickly and throw so it bursts in mid-air by the wall.

steps.text: Shoot the Eye Switch above the burning platform with the Slingshot to douse the flames, jump across and go down the hallway of Baby Dodongos to the door at the end.
steps.detail: The flames return after a moment; jump as soon as they vanish. Keep the shield up in the hallway and the Baby Dodongos hop over you.

steps.text: In the upper Lizalfos room, defeat both Lizalfos on the small platforms to open the next door, then go through.
steps.detail: Same tactics as before, but watch your footing over the lava. Recovery Hearts are on the side platform if you need them.

steps.text: Shoot the Eye Switch to put out the first flame, jump to the first platform, then shoot the second Eye Switch in the alcove to the left to put out the second flame and cross.
Back in the upper part of the Blade Trap room, jump to the next platform, climb the ledge on your right and open the big chest for the Bombs.
steps.detail: You get a Bomb Bag holding 20 Bombs. Ignore the cracked wall one level down; it hides two Business Scrubs selling Deku Nuts and Deku Seeds.

steps.text: Continue into the last part of the main room's second floor and step on the floor switch to raise the lift, creating a shortcut up to this floor.
Read the stone tablet by the switch, then head right onto the bridge above the giant Dodongo skull.
steps.detail: The poem says to light the skull's eyes red. Optional: bomb the cracked wall along the way for a small chest with a Red Rupee.

steps.text: Stand at each of the two holes in the bridge and drop a Bomb down (press the Bomb button twice) so it explodes on the eye below; once both eyes glow red the skull's jaw drops, revealing a door.
steps.detail: Do one eye, wait for the blast, then the other. The eyes stay lit.

steps.text: Get down to the main floor: drop from the bridge onto the top of the skull, then onto the platform below.
steps.detail: Or take the lift or the long way around if you prefer.

steps.text: Facing the skull, go through the farthest doorway on the right side back into the Baby Dodongo corridor, follow the right wall to the cracked wall and bomb it open.
In the small room behind it, kill the three Keese and the Gold Skulltula, then jump-attack or backflip up to grab its token.
steps.detail: A Bomb tossed at the group takes them all out. The token sits high on the wall; a jump attack or a backflip beneath it snags it.

steps.text: Return to the main room and walk into the open mouth of the Dodongo skull.
In the square room beyond, hop down, kill the Fire Keese if they bother you, then climb up on the right side and follow the long hallway.
steps.detail: The boss door here is barred for now; the block that opens it is found by looping through the next rooms.

steps.text: In the S-shaped room, shoot the two Fire Keese, drop down and work your way to the far side, climbing over the stone blocks in the way.
Bomb the cracked wall on the ledge at the far end of the S-shaped room and go through the door.
steps.detail: Throw the Bomb up onto the ledge, or hold it until it flashes fast and throw so it explodes against the wall.

steps.text: Defeat the Armos in the small room and grab the Gold Skulltula token it was guarding, then return to the S-shaped room.
steps.detail: Deku Nut, jump attack, then shield or run from the explosion. The Gold Skulltula is behind where the statue stood.

steps.text: Use the stone blocks to climb onto the high wall in the S-shaped room, run along its top and drop into the next area, then continue down the hallway.
steps.detail: The Fire Keese respawn; shoot them again if needed. A jar on the left of the drop-down area holds a Fairy you can bottle.

steps.text: On the upper ledge of the square room, push the stone block off the edge, then drop down and kill the two Fire Keese.
Push the stone block onto the switch in the hole in the center of the square room to hold the boss door open.
Go through the boss door, bomb the cracked patch on the floor and open the chest for Bombs, then drop through the hole to face the boss.
steps.detail: Top up so you enter with a full bag.

steps.text: Defeat King Dodongo.
steps.detail: When he opens his mouth to inhale before breathing fire, throw a Bomb (or a Bomb Flower from the edge of the arena) into it; he swallows it, is stunned, and you slash him. He then rolls around the arena: stand in an inside corner or near the lava edge, or hold your shield. Repeat four or five times. A jump attack as he lands after the stun deals extra damage.

steps.text: Take the Heart Container and step into the blue light to leave Dodongo's Cavern.
Watch the scene outside: Darunia names you Sworn Brothers and gives you the Goron's Ruby, the second Spiritual Stone.
steps.detail: He tells you to visit the Great Fairy at the top of the mountain, which comes after some cleanup. Step aside from the two Gorons who drop in for a hug.

steps.text: Head down the trail toward Kakariko Village, bomb the cracked wall where you hear a Gold Skulltula, shoot the Skulltula and climb the wall behind it for the token.
steps.detail: The cracked wall is on the side of the trail between Dodongo's Cavern and the Kakariko gate. Kill the spider with the Slingshot first, then climb the stone face to reach the token.

steps.text: Go back up the trail toward Goron City and bomb the second cracked wall on the way; open the chest behind it for a Purple Rupee.
In Goron City, wait for the rolling Hot Rodder Goron to enter the enclosed tunnel section on the north side and stop him there with a Bomb; he rewards you with a bigger Bomb Bag.
steps.detail: He rolls laps around one tier and runs you over if you stand in his path. Drop the Bomb just ahead of him inside the covered stretch so it bursts as he passes. If he stops anywhere else he just grumbles; try again on the next lap. Capacity goes up to 30 Bombs.

steps.text: Go to the top tier of Goron City and bomb the three boulders blocking the path on the west side.
steps.detail: You can also tightrope across the ropes to the pedestal, but bombing is faster.

steps.text: Follow the short path to the boulder maze and bomb through the normal boulders, keeping right for the first half and then the middle, opening the small chests for Purple Rupees along the way.
steps.detail: The silver boulders cannot be broken yet; leave them.

steps.text: Roll into the wooden crate at the back of the maze to free a Gold Skulltula, kill it and take its token. Then leave Goron City.
Back on the trail, return to where the path splits and take the branch climbing to the highest point; bomb the first boulder blocking the way.
Bomb the second boulder (hold the Bomb until it is about to explode, then throw it), jump over and pick up the Red Rupee that was under it.
Climb up and bomb the boulder there to uncover a hole with a cow inside; drop in and play Epona's Song for Lon Lon Milk if you want a refill.
steps.detail: Optional. The cow gives milk any time you play Epona's Song next to it with an empty bottle.

steps.text: Keep going up; when the volcano erupts, hold the Hylian Shield up and cross between bursts of falling rocks until it stops.
steps.detail: Hold R to block the debris and run during the gaps. It stops once you get close to the other side.

steps.text: Shoot the Skullwalltulas on the climbable wall with the Slingshot, then climb to the top of Death Mountain.
At the summit, ignore Kaepora Gaebora for now and enter the opening in the mountain on the right, into Death Mountain Crater.
Roll into the wooden crate right at the entrance of Death Mountain Crater, kill the Gold Skulltula inside and take its token.
steps.detail: The heat timer runs while you are inside; if it reaches zero you lose all your hearts, so watch it.

steps.text: Exit and re-enter to reset the heat timer, then run to the ledge, line up facing the Triforce platform below and run straight off the cliff; Link grabs the climbable wall.
Climb down the wall to the small alcove partway down and pick up the Piece of Heart there.
steps.detail: You cannot climb back up in time, so jump into the lava afterward: you lose one heart and reappear at the crater entrance.

steps.text: Leave Death Mountain Crater.
At the summit, place a Bomb against the cracked wall to open the Great Fairy Fountain and go in.
Stand on the Triforce symbol and play Zelda's Lullaby; the Great Fairy of Power gives you the Magic Meter and the spin attack.
steps.detail: Hold B to charge a spin attack; it uses magic. She also mentions her friend near Hyrule Castle, visited later this chapter.

steps.text: Outside, talk to Kaepora Gaebora, then stand beneath him when he finishes; he flies you down to a rooftop in Kakariko Village.
On the rooftop where the owl drops you, walk to the right edge above the Cucco pen and drop onto the thatched overhang below, then turn around and enter the hole in the wall of the house.
steps.detail: Do not jump off the main roof yet. If you do fall, play the Sun's Song before leaving the village to reappear on the roof, or ride the owl down again.

steps.text: Inside the house with the caged cow, pick up the Piece of Heart.
Go to the Market and enter the Bombchu Bowling Alley, on the same side as the Shooting Gallery, between the Hyrule Field exit and the road to Hyrule Castle.
steps.detail: Each game costs 30 Rupees; smash the pots in the guardhouse by the field exit for Rupees if you run low.

steps.text: Play Bombchu Bowling until you win the Piece of Heart.
steps.detail: First wall: line up perfectly straight and release when the path is clear. Second wall: angle about 45 degrees and let the Bombchu climb the side wall. Last wall: release when the big Cucco is off to one side. Prizes cycle in order: Bombchus, Piece of Heart, Bombs, Bomb Bag, Purple Rupee; the first prize is random, then they follow that order.

steps.text: Keep playing Bombchu Bowling until you win the Bomb Bag upgrade.
steps.detail: It raises your capacity to 40 Bombs. If you win the Purple Rupee first, the cycle wraps back to Bombchus, so keep going.

steps.text: Go to Hyrule Castle, climb the vines by the gate, go straight ahead, jump down and bomb the boulder behind the Dead End sign, then crawl through the hole.
steps.detail: Same vines you used to sneak in earlier; the boulder is in the corner where the sign stands.

steps.text: Stand on the Triforce symbol and play Zelda's Lullaby; the Great Fairy of Magic gives you Din's Fire.
steps.detail: Din's Fire lights every torch around you at once and burns nearby enemies; it costs magic. You need the Magic Meter from Death Mountain first.

steps.text: In the southwest of Hyrule Field, by the entrance to Lake Hylia, drop a Bomb in the exact middle of the four square fences to open a hidden grotto and drop in.
steps.detail: Stand centered between the four fenced squares. If you have the Stone of Agony, the controller rumbles on the spot.

steps.text: Talk to the Business Scrub in the grotto and pay 10 Rupees for the Piece of Heart.
Go through the Lost Woods to the last clearing before the Sacred Forest Meadow and bomb the boulder there to open a grotto.
steps.detail: From the Kokiri Forest entrance: right, left, right, left, straight, left, right reaches the meadow entrance; the boulder is in that final clearing. Or use the Goron City shortcut.
