steps.text: Drop in and buy the Deku Nut upgrade from the first Business Scrub for 40 Rupees.
steps.detail: Your Deku Nut capacity rises to 30. The second scrub only sells regular goods.
steps.missable: Buy this before adult Link obtains the Poacher's Saw in the trading sequence; after that, this Business Scrub never offers the upgrade again.

steps.text: From Hyrule Field, follow the river upstream from the Market drawbridge and go through the gap in the cliff into Zora's River.
steps.detail: The entrance sits on the east side of Hyrule Field, between Kokiri Forest and Kakariko Village. Run forward as you arrive and Kaepora Gaebora swoops down: the short version is that you play Zelda's Lullaby at the far end of the river to get into Zora's Domain.

steps.text: Roll into the first tree on your left just past the entrance to shake a Gold Skulltula loose, kill it and take the token.
steps.detail: Run at the trunk and press A to roll into it. The spider drops to the ground; one sword slash or a Slingshot seed finishes it, then walk over the token.

steps.text: Bomb the boulders blocking the river path and walk through the rubble.
steps.detail: Set the Bomb against the middle boulder and back off. A Cucco is pecking about just beyond them; leave it there for now, you come back for it shortly.

steps.text: Round the corner and buy a Magic Bean from the Magic Bean Salesman sitting by the water.
steps.detail: The first bean costs 10 Rupees and every later one costs 10 more. This is the only place in the game that sells them and adult Link needs the grown plants to reach several Heart Pieces, so buy as many as your wallet holds.

steps.text: Plant a Magic Bean in the patch of soft soil right beside the salesman.
steps.detail: Stand on the dark soil, put the bean on a C button and press A. Nothing happens until you come back as an adult, when it becomes a flying platform. This is the only soft soil in the game with no Gold Skulltula under it, so do not waste bugs on it.

steps.text: For more bean money, travel to Kakariko Village and drop a Bomb on the rattling patch of ground just past the first tree inside the entrance.
steps.detail: Walk the area slowly: the Stone of Agony buzzes when you stand on the right spot. The Bomb blows open a hidden grotto.

steps.text: Drop into the grotto and kill the two ReDead inside.
steps.detail: Their scream freezes you on the spot. Play the Sun's Song as you land to paralyse both of them, then slash away freely. Without it, keep your distance and hit them as they shuffle toward you.

steps.text: Open the chest in the grotto for a Gold Rupee worth 200 Rupees, then take the green warp out.
steps.detail: With the Adult's Wallet you can hold all 200. Anything over your cap is simply lost, so spend before you collect if your wallet is nearly full.

steps.text: Go back to the Magic Bean Salesman in Zora's River and spend the Rupees on as many more beans as you can afford.
steps.detail: There are ten soft soil spots in Hyrule and every bean bought now is one you do not pay a steeper price for later. Plant them as you pass each patch in later chapters.

steps.text: Walk back to the Cucco past the bombed boulders and pick it up.
steps.detail: Carrying the Cucco is the only way to reach the two Heart Pieces in this area as a child. If it ends up in the water it flies back to this spot, so you can always come and fetch it again.

steps.text: Jump across to the far bank of the river and follow it upstream to the bend.
steps.detail: An Octorok pops up in the water and spits rocks. Just keep running past it; with a Cucco in your hands you cannot swing the sword anyway.

steps.text: Jump back over the river where it narrows, then follow the path left over the small gap into the wide open area.
steps.detail: Blue Tektites hop around the water here. They lunge at you in a straight line, so sidestep and keep moving toward the far end of the area.

steps.text: At the north end of the area, take a running jump off the ledge against the wall and let go of the Cucco in mid-air so it carries you onto the low platform in the water.
steps.detail: Aim at the platform, press A to jump off the edge and release the Cucco the moment you are over the gap. If you drop into the water the Cucco returns to the start of the area and you fetch it again.

steps.text: Climb up and hop across to the top of the stone pillar for a Piece of Heart.
steps.detail: The pillar is the tall one standing in the middle of the water. Land on the platform first, then make the short hop up.

steps.text: Drop back down, fetch the Cucco and carry it right along the bank past the Blue Tektites.
steps.detail: The Cucco is waiting back at the boulders if it fell in the water on the way down.

steps.text: At the first tall platform, throw the Cucco up onto it, climb up after it and pick it up again.
steps.detail: Face the ledge and press A to toss the bird up; it lands and waits. Then grab the edge and pull yourself up.

steps.text: Wade right through the water to the second platform and repeat: throw the Cucco up, climb after it, pick it up.
steps.detail: Same trick as the last ledge. Keep hold of the Cucco from here to the waterfall.

steps.text: Cross the water to the left and follow the path over the wooden bridge into the area of stepped platforms below the waterfall.
steps.detail: This is the last stretch of the river. The platforms zigzag up toward the roaring waterfall at the back.

steps.text: Hop onto the platform on your right and climb the stack up to the highest one, right in front of the waterfall.
steps.detail: Take the jumps one at a time and aim for the centre of each platform. Falling only costs you the climb back up.

steps.text: Stand on the highest platform, turn around to face the lone platform in the corner and glide over to it with the Cucco for a Piece of Heart.
steps.detail: The target platform sits by itself across the gap behind you, with nothing else near it. Run off the edge holding the Cucco and steer with the stick while you float.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to turn it to night.
steps.detail: The Gold Skulltula below only comes out after dark. Play it again later if you want daylight back.

steps.text: Drop into the shallow water by the ladder near the waterfall and shoot the Gold Skulltula on the ladder with the Fairy Slingshot, then collect the token.
steps.detail: You hear it clicking before you see it. Z-target the spider, hit it with a seed and it falls; the token lands in the shallow water below.

steps.text: Climb onto the square grated platform in front of the waterfall and play Zelda's Lullaby.
steps.detail: The grate is the flat Triforce-marked block on the topmost ledge facing the falls. The water parts and reveals the tunnel behind it.

steps.text: Jump across the gap into the opening behind the parted waterfall to enter Zora's Domain.
steps.detail: Take a running jump from the grate. If you fall you land in the water below and have to climb the platforms again; the waterfall stays open.

steps.text: Smash the pots along the spiral ramp until you have a Deku Stick.
steps.detail: You need one burning stick to light five torches for the Piece of Heart here. If you run out mid-run there are more pots along the ramp.

steps.text: Go to the top of the Domain and light your Deku Stick on the burning torch near King Zora.
steps.detail: This is the only flame already lit in the Domain. A stick burns for about a minute, so plan the route down before you light it; if it burns out, come back up here and start again.

steps.text: Run down the ramp and light the first unlit torch with the burning stick.
steps.detail: Touch the torch with the stick held out. The flame stays lit as long as you light the rest before too long.

steps.text: Keep going down and light the torch in front of the Zora Shop.
steps.detail: Second of five. Do not stop to browse the shop; the stick is burning.

steps.text: Light the torch standing in the water by the ring of stones at the bottom.
steps.detail: Third of five. Wade, do not swim: swimming puts the stick out.

steps.text: Run into the alcove behind the waterfall and light the last two torches there.
steps.detail: They stand side by side, so one pass lights both. With all five burning at once a large chest appears in the alcove.

steps.text: Open the big chest that appears behind the waterfall for a Piece of Heart.
steps.detail: If no chest appeared, one of the five torches went out before the last was lit. Grab another Deku Stick and run the route faster.

steps.text: Go back to the top of the Domain, take the path left of King Zora up to the top of the waterfall and talk to the Zora standing there.
steps.detail: He runs a diving game: he throws Rupees into the pool below and you have 50 seconds to fetch them all.

steps.text: Pay the 20 Rupees, jump off the waterfall and dive with A until you have collected all five Rupees before the timer runs out.
steps.detail: You can swim while underwater, so line up two Rupees on one dive. Use Z to straighten yourself out if you lose your bearings. If the timer beats you, just pay and try again.

steps.text: Climb back up to the Zora at the top of the waterfall and talk to him to receive the Silver Scale.
steps.detail: The Silver Scale lets you dive much deeper, which is what opens the tunnel at the bottom of this pool and a lot of underwater treasure later on.

steps.text: Dive to the deepest part of the pool at the bottom of the Domain and swim through the hole in the wall down there.
steps.detail: It comes out in Lake Hylia. Reaching it needs the Silver Scale from the diving game; if you skipped that, leave through Zora's River and cross Hyrule Field to Lake Hylia on foot instead.

steps.text: Surface in Lake Hylia and swim over to the broken stone pillars near the shore, where Navi flies off and glows green.
steps.detail: The tunnel drops you into the lake near the ruins. Navi parks herself over the spot in the water.

steps.text: Dive down at that spot and grab the bottle floating there: it holds Ruto's Letter.
steps.detail: Press A while swimming to dive. The bottle and the letter count as one item until you show the letter to King Zora, after which the bottle is yours to use.

steps.text: Swim back to the underwater hole by the ruins and go through it to return to Zora's Domain.
steps.detail: Same tunnel, other direction, and it needs the Silver Scale as well. Without it, walk out of Lake Hylia into Hyrule Field and go back around through Zora's River.

steps.text: Climb to King Zora's platform and show him the bottle with Ruto's Letter.
steps.detail: Stand in front of the throne and use the bottle from a C button. He reads it, shuffles aside over a long, long scene and clears the passage behind him to Zora's Fountain. Your bottle is now empty.

steps.text: Dive back down to the shallow water at the bottom of the Domain and scoop a fish into the empty bottle.
steps.detail: The fish circle around the ring of stones. Swim up to one and use the empty bottle to catch it. You need the fish to get into Jabu-Jabu; the shop also sells one for 200 Rupees if you would rather not chase them.

steps.text: Go back to the top of the Domain and walk through the passage King Zora was sitting in front of, into Zora's Fountain.
steps.detail: It is the short tunnel directly behind the throne.

steps.text: Swim to the small island in the southeast corner of the Fountain and roll into the lone tree to knock down a Gold Skulltula, then take the token.
steps.detail: The island is the patch of land off to the right as you look at Jabu-Jabu. Roll into the trunk, kill the spider on the ground and walk over the token.

steps.text: Set a Bomb beside the silver boulder against the wall on that island to blow open the cave behind it.
steps.detail: You cannot lift a silver boulder until you are an adult with the Silver Gauntlets, but the cracked wall behind it means a Bomb works just as well.

steps.text: Go into the cave and play Zelda's Lullaby standing on the Triforce tile to summon the Great Fairy of Magic, who gives you Farore's Wind.
steps.detail: Farore's Wind drops a warp point you can teleport back to; it only works inside dungeons, but it saves a lot of walking in the long ones ahead.

steps.text: Swim north across the Fountain and climb out on the ledge in front of Lord Jabu-Jabu.
steps.detail: Jabu-Jabu is the enormous fish floating at the back of the Fountain. The Zoras below mention he expects an offering.

steps.text: Stand in front of Jabu-Jabu's mouth and drop the fish out of the bottle; he inhales you and the dungeon starts.
steps.detail: Select the bottled fish and press A while facing him to set it down. You can walk back out of the dungeon later through his teeth at any time.

steps.text: Step forward into the Mouth and deal with the two Octoroks that pop out of the water.
steps.detail: Hold up the Deku Shield to bounce their rocks straight back at them, or dodge and shoot them with the Fairy Slingshot. They stay in the water, so keep to the walkway.

steps.text: Head down the corridor ahead, clearing the floating Shaboms out of the way.
steps.detail: Shaboms are the drifting bubbles. A thrown Deku Nut pops every one nearby at once; the sword works too but you have to chase them.

steps.text: At the narrow end of the corridor, shoot the small nub hanging from the ceiling with the Fairy Slingshot to open the veiny door.
steps.detail: Navi flies to it to point it out. Z-target the nub first, then fire; the door ahead peels open.

steps.text: Go through the door into the Throat and follow the ledge around the room to the far side.
steps.detail: This is the tall room with the spiked platform running up and down it. The floating electric jellyfish are Biri: do not touch them, just walk around. A Deku Nut kills one if it is in your way.

steps.text: Take the door on the opposite side of the Throat into the Upper Stomach.
steps.detail: The Upper Stomach is the big open room with holes in the floor. It becomes the hub of the dungeon.

steps.text: Talk to Princess Ruto in the middle of the room and sit through the argument; she storms off and falls through a hole in the floor.
steps.detail: She insists she knows nothing about a letter and wants no help at all. Nothing you say changes the scene.

steps.text: Drop through the hole Ruto fell down to reach the Lower Stomach.
steps.detail: It is the open hole in the floor where she vanished. You land on a platform beside her.

steps.text: Talk to Ruto over and over until she stops complaining and curls up so you can carry her.
steps.detail: Keep pressing A through every line. She mentions a precious stone, which is the Spiritual Stone of Water you came for. If she ever drowns or you leave a room without her, she reappears where you last picked her up.

steps.text: Pick Ruto up and carry her through the door on this platform before the Biri drift over.
steps.detail: Stand against her and press A to lift her. You cannot use the sword while carrying her, so move rather than fight.

steps.text: Clear the Shaboms out of the corridor beyond the door.
steps.detail: One Deku Nut pops the lot. You can also throw Ruto at them, which works and costs nothing but her dignity.

steps.text: Round the corner and drop down into the shallow pit of water below.
steps.detail: The far side of the pit is too high to climb, which is the puzzle: you need the water level raised.

steps.text: Kill the Stingers burrowed in the floor of the pit.
steps.detail: Throw Ruto at a Stinger while it is still buried and it dies in one hit. Do this now while the water is low; they are miserable to dodge once you are swimming.

steps.text: Throw Ruto up onto the high ledge on the far side of the pit so the rising water cannot reach her.
steps.detail: Face the ledge and press A. If she ends up in the water she is sent back to where you first picked her up and you have to fetch her.

steps.text: Step on the floor switch in the middle of the pit to raise the water level.
steps.detail: The water rises to just under the far ledge, so you can swim up and climb out.

steps.text: Shoot the Gold Skulltula on the side wall of this room with the Fairy Slingshot and collect its token.
steps.detail: Look up the wall above the pit. Kill it first, then swim or climb to where the token is hanging and grab it.

steps.text: Swim up with the raised water and pull yourself out on the far ledge.
steps.detail: Press A against the edge to climb out next to Ruto.

steps.text: Pick Ruto back up and carry her along the next corridor, popping the Shaboms as you go.
steps.detail: Deku Nut again, or wait a moment for them to drift out of the narrow part.

steps.text: At the closed door, set Ruto down and shoot the nub on the ceiling with the Fairy Slingshot to open it.
steps.detail: Same kind of switch as before. You cannot aim the Slingshot with her in your arms, which is why she goes down first.

steps.text: Pick Ruto up and go through the door into the Throat.
steps.detail: You come out on the lower ledge of the tall spiked-platform room.

steps.text: Put Ruto down and bounce the Octorok's rock back at it with the Deku Shield.
steps.detail: Hold R facing the Octorok and its own rock kills it. Trying to tank the hit while holding Ruto just makes you drop her.

steps.text: Dive through the hole in the wall straight ahead to the Business Scrub, bounce his nut back with the shield and buy Deku Nuts for 20 Rupees.
steps.detail: Deku Nuts are the fastest answer to Shaboms and Biri for the rest of the dungeon, so it is worth the detour if you are low.

steps.text: Pick Ruto up, wait for the spiked platform to come down to your ledge and step on as it passes.
steps.detail: Stand clear of the spikes on the underside and board the flat top. It carries you back up to the small hallway you were in earlier.

steps.text: Hop off the platform onto the upper ledge and take the door back into the Upper Stomach.
steps.detail: This is the room where you first met Ruto, and from now on it is where she reappears whenever you lose her.

steps.text: Carry Ruto across the Upper Stomach to the door on the opposite side, the one you have not used yet.
steps.detail: Biri drop from the ceiling on the way and so do Bari, the bigger jellyfish that split into three Biri when killed. You cannot fight while carrying Ruto, so walk a wide line around them.

steps.text: Go through that door into the long branching hallway.
steps.detail: Several doors here are shut for now. The floating electric worms are Tailpasarans and nothing you own can hurt them yet, so keep clear of them.

steps.text: Carry Ruto to the floor switch on the right-hand branch and stand on it while still holding her; the extra weight presses it all the way down and opens the door.
steps.detail: Your own weight alone is not enough. Step on with Ruto in your arms and the door beside the switch grinds open and stays open.

steps.text: Carry Ruto through the door the switch opened, into the small Stinger room.
steps.detail: A cramped square room with nothing visible in it at first.

steps.text: Set Ruto down by the door and kill the four Stingers that burst out of the floor.
steps.detail: They pop up one at a time and charge. Z-target, sidestep the charge and slash. With her on the ground you have the sword free.

steps.text: Open the large chest that appears in the middle of the room for the Boomerang.
steps.detail: The Boomerang stuns most enemies, kills small ones, cuts the parasitic tentacles ahead and pulls in distant items, which is how you finally reach several Gold Skulltula tokens.

steps.text: Put the Boomerang on a C button, pick Ruto back up and leave through the same door.
steps.detail: Test a throw on the way out: it flies where you aim, hits and comes back with anything it touched.

steps.text: Carry Ruto across the hallway to the floor switch on the other branch, set her down on top of it and leave her there holding it down.
steps.detail: This switch springs back the moment weight comes off it, and the door only stays open while it is pressed. Ruto sitting on it is the trick. She sulks about it afterwards.

steps.text: Go through the door the switch opened, into the Red Tail room, without Ruto.
steps.detail: Navi warns you about the thing growing out of the wall inside.

steps.text: Kill the Parasitic Tentacle: Z-target it, circle around it and keep throwing the Boomerang into it.
steps.detail: The Boomerang is the only thing that cuts it. Stay moving as you throw; standing still lets it swat you across the room. Four or five clean hits finish it.

steps.text: Open the large chest left behind for the Dungeon Map.
steps.detail: The room is only reachable while Ruto can weigh the springy switch down. Once she is gone there is no way back in on this visit.
steps.missable: Get the Dungeon Map now. Once Ruto is carried down to Big Octo's Lair you can never press the switch outside this room again, and the chest is unreachable for the rest of the game.

steps.text: Leave the Red Tail room and step back out into the hallway, where Ruto is waiting and annoyed.
steps.detail: From here on she vanishes back to the Upper Stomach whenever you leave a room without her, which is fine: you do not need her again until the very end of this floor.

steps.text: Round the corner in the hallway and go through the nearby door into the Shabom room.
steps.detail: Navi points out that the tentacle blocking this door is gone. This side room holds the Compass.

steps.text: Pop every Shabom in the room within the 40 second limit.
steps.detail: Z-target and throw the Boomerang, which takes several at once on the return trip; a spin attack clears a cluster. Miss the timer and you are dumped back at the start of the room with less health.

steps.text: Open the chest that appears for the Compass, then head back out into the hallway.
steps.detail: The Compass marks the chests and the boss on the map.

steps.text: Cross back to the far side of the hallway and go through the door right next to the Boomerang room.
steps.detail: It is the Blue Tail room, open now that the first tentacle is dead.

steps.text: Kill the second Parasitic Tentacle with the Boomerang the same way.
steps.detail: No enemies to bother you in here. Circle and throw.

steps.text: Leave the room and go to the middle door of the hallway, into the Green Tail room.
steps.detail: The last of the three tentacles is in here, and this one has company.

steps.text: Kill the Biri floating around the tentacle first.
steps.detail: The tentacle knocks you straight into them if you ignore them. A Deku Nut or a Boomerang throw takes each one out.

steps.text: Destroy the third Parasitic Tentacle with the Boomerang; the door unlocks when it dies.
steps.detail: With all three dead, the tentacle blocking one of the holes in the Upper Stomach disappears.

steps.text: Leave the Green Tail room and go back up the hallway into the Upper Stomach.
steps.detail: Ruto is waiting for you in the middle of that room.

steps.text: Pick Ruto up in the Upper Stomach.
steps.detail: Talk to her first if she is standing rather than curled up.

steps.text: Carry Ruto to the hole in the far corner, opposite the one she originally fell down, and drop through it onto the new platform below.
steps.detail: A tentacle used to block this hole and is gone now that all three are dead. This is the point of no return for the Dungeon Map: if you have not opened that chest, go back and do it before you take Ruto down here, because you can never hold the springy switch down again.

steps.text: Kill the nearer of the two Gold Skulltulas on the wall here and pull its token in with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: Set Ruto down first. Throw the Boomerang at the spider to kill it, then throw again at the token to reel it in from across the gap.

steps.text: Kill the second Gold Skulltula further along the same wall and pull that token in with the Boomerang too.
steps.detail: Same routine: one throw to kill, one throw to collect.

steps.text: Pick Ruto up, follow the only corridor off this platform and go through the door at the end into Big Octo's Lair.
steps.detail: A round room with a spinning spiked track and a platform in the centre.

steps.text: Throw Ruto onto the platform in the middle of the room as she demands; she grabs the Spiritual Stone of Water and is carried up out of reach.
steps.detail: Stand at the edge facing the platform and press A. The scene plays out whether you like it or not, and then the mini-boss shows up.

steps.text: Mini-boss: stun Big Octo with the Boomerang and slash his backside with the sword until he dies.
steps.detail: He charges around the spiked track at your running speed. The easy method: stun him with the Boomerang, wait for the stun to wear off, let him turn away, stun him again and hit the soft back end. He only takes damage from behind. Four slashes, or two jump attacks, finish him.

steps.text: Pick up the hearts he drops, then step onto the central platform to ride it up to the next level.
steps.detail: The platform only rises once Big Octo is dead.

steps.text: Kill the Biri along the upper ledge and take the only exit from this level.
steps.detail: Boomerang throws handle them from a safe distance. There is a fairy in a jar up here if you need healing or an empty bottle filled.

steps.text: Stand on the platform by the door you came in and hit the first big red jellyfish with the Boomerang; it freezes solid.
steps.detail: Frozen, it works as a stepping stone. There is an Octorok in the water below that can knock you off mid-jump, so shoot it first if it is bothering you.

steps.text: Jump onto the frozen jellyfish and stun the second one ahead of you with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: The freeze wears off after a few seconds, so line up the next throw as soon as you land.

steps.text: Jump across to the second frozen jellyfish and on to the ledge with the door, then go through it.
steps.detail: If a jellyfish thaws while you are on it you drop into the water below and have to climb back and start the jumps again.

steps.text: In the Throat, jump onto the lone platform across the gap; it sinks under your weight and links up with the ledge by the unused door.
steps.detail: The platform lowers as soon as you land on it, forming the bridge across.

steps.text: Carry one of the wooden boxes from the ledge onto the floor switch to hold the door open.
steps.detail: The switch springs back up when you step off it and Ruto is not here to sit on it any more. Lift a box with A and set it down squarely on the switch.

steps.text: Go through the door the box opened, into the Biri room.
steps.detail: The last room before the boss, full of drifting electric jellyfish.

steps.text: Kill all the Biri drifting around the room.
steps.detail: Boomerang throws take them out one at a time from a distance without any risk of the shock.

steps.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula on the vines at the far side of the room and take its token as you go by.
steps.detail: Boomerang the spider off the vines, then grab the token; if it is stuck high on the wall, throw the Boomerang at it to pull it in.

steps.text: Climb the vines to the ledge at the top.
steps.detail: Face the vines and press A to grab on, then climb with the stick.

steps.text: Z-target the switch nub hanging from the ceiling behind the web barrier and hit it with the Boomerang; the boss door opens.
steps.detail: The Boomerang curves past the web where a Slingshot seed cannot. It may take two or three throws to find the angle, so keep the target locked and retry.

steps.text: Go through the boss door.
steps.detail: Heal up first: break the pots around the room for hearts and bottle a fairy if you have an empty bottle.

steps.text: Phase one: cut Barinade's three tentacles off the ceiling with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: He hangs from the ceiling draining Jabu-Jabu. Z-target one tentacle at a time and keep circling the room while you throw, so the electric beams sweep past behind you.

steps.text: Phase two: stun the main body with the Boomerang to break its link to the orbiting jellyfish, then kill the jellyfish.
steps.detail: While the link is live they are invincible and touching it hurts. One Boomerang hit on the body cuts the link for a few seconds; kill the loose jellyfish with Deku Nuts, the Boomerang or the sword, then stun him again.

steps.text: Phase three: keep hitting the spinning body with the Boomerang, then wipe out the second ring of jellyfish.
steps.detail: He now zips around the room with the jellyfish spinning tight around him and he can shoot even while stunned. Run in, throw a Deku Nut to take several at once, and back off.

steps.text: Phase four: stun the bare body with the Boomerang and slash it with the sword until Barinade explodes.
steps.detail: With no jellyfish left he moves faster and fires more often. Stun him, run in, get two or three slashes before he sinks into the floor, then keep away until he rises again. Around ten slashes in total.

steps.text: Take the Heart Container, then step into the blue light with Ruto to leave Jabu-Jabu's Belly.
steps.detail: The Heart Container adds a full heart permanently. Ruto has some words for you about how long you took.

steps.text: Watch the scene outside: Ruto hands over the Zora's Sapphire, the Spiritual Stone of Water.
steps.detail: Either answer works; she treats it as an engagement gift regardless. You end up floating in the water in Zora's Fountain with the third Spiritual Stone.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to turn it to night.
steps.detail: The last Gold Skulltula here only appears after dark.

steps.text: Swim to the log arching out of the water just south of Jabu-Jabu, stand on it and take the Gold Skulltula off the wall with the Boomerang, then collect the token.
steps.detail: The log is on Jabu-Jabu's left, near the way back to Zora's Domain. Throw once to kill the spider and once more to reel the token in.

steps.text: Travel to Kokiri Forest and go back inside the Great Deku Tree.
steps.detail: The entrance is still open. You are after one Gold Skulltula in a room you could not enter on the first visit.

steps.text: Work your way down to B1 and go to the northwest corner of that floor, where a spider web covers a doorway.
steps.detail: B1 is the floor with the burnable web over the hole in the middle. Follow the outer walkway around to the northwest side.

steps.text: Burn the web away with a Deku Stick lit at the nearest torch, or with Din's Fire.
steps.detail: Din's Fire is faster and cannot burn out on the way. With a stick, light it at a torch on this floor and run straight to the web.

steps.text: Bomb the boulder sitting behind the web to clear the doorway.
steps.detail: Set the Bomb against the boulder and stand back.

steps.text: Step into the room and take the Gold Skulltula off the wall with the Boomerang, then pull in the token.
steps.detail: One throw kills the spider, a second throw reels the token in from the wall.

steps.text: Leave the Great Deku Tree and travel to Lon Lon Ranch; play the Sun's Song if it is not night yet.
steps.detail: Both Skulltulas here only come out after dark. The ranch gate stays open at night for child Link.

steps.text: Just inside the ranch entrance, kill the Gold Skulltula on the window of the building on the left and collect the token with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: It is high on the window frame of the house to your left as you walk in, out of sword reach.

steps.text: Cross to the far southwest side of the ranch and take the Gold Skulltula high on the edge of the wall there with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: Walk the perimeter of the field; you hear it clicking before you see it up on the rim.

steps.text: Go out to Hyrule Field and head west to the ring of stones near the Gerudo Valley bridge; stand in the middle where the Stone of Agony rattles and drop a Bomb.
steps.detail: The circle of rocks is out in the open field just short of the valley entrance. The Bomb opens a grotto in the ground.

steps.text: Drop into the grotto and burn all the spider webs inside with Din's Fire to reach the cow.
steps.detail: Stand in the middle of the webbed area and cast Din's Fire; it clears several webs in one go. You can play Epona's Song to the cow for milk if you have a bottle free.

steps.text: Take the Gold Skulltula on the wall above and behind the cow with the Boomerang, then pull the token in.
steps.detail: Stand back from the cow so you have a clear line at the spider high on the wall.

steps.text: Climb out and cross the bridge into Gerudo Valley.
steps.detail: Still night. Child Link can walk in as far as the tent and the ramps.

steps.text: Walk up to the wooden ramp, turn right to the water pouring out of the hole in the cliff and take the Gold Skulltula there with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: It crawls on the rock around the spout. Kill it with one throw and collect the token with a second.

steps.text: Travel to Lake Hylia and walk onto the bridge by the Lakeside Laboratory at the northwest of the lake.
steps.detail: Still night. Stand on the planks facing the laboratory building.

steps.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall of the Lakeside Laboratory and pull the token in with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: It sits on the side of the building above the water, too high to reach any other way.

steps.text: Go back to Hyrule Field and find the lone tree just north of the small bridge between the Market and Kakariko Village; bomb the ground where the Stone of Agony rattles.
steps.detail: Walk slow circles around the tree until the controller rattles, then drop the Bomb on that spot to open a grotto.

steps.text: Drop into the grotto and kill the big Skulltula guarding it.
steps.detail: It blocks the way with its armoured front. Wait for it to spin around and slash the soft back, or stun it with a Deku Nut first.

steps.text: Take the Gold Skulltula higher up on the grotto wall with the Boomerang and pull the token in.
steps.detail: Look up once the big one is dead; it is on the wall above where the big Skulltula was sitting.

steps.text: Travel to Kakariko Village and go into the Graveyard; play the Sun's Song if it has turned to day.
steps.detail: Head for the southeast corner of the Graveyard, to the right of the entrance as you come in.

steps.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall in the southeast corner of the Graveyard and collect the token with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: It crawls high on the stone wall at night. Throw once to kill and once to reel the token in.

steps.text: Go up Death Mountain Trail and back into Dodongo's Cavern.
steps.detail: The last Gold Skulltula of this tour sits at the top of the big staircase room, and getting there means taking the long way around the cavern again.

steps.text: In the main room, ride the tall pillar platform up to 2F.
steps.detail: Stand on the pillar near the middle of the room and wait for it to carry you up.

steps.text: Take the west door off 2F into the next room.
steps.detail: The door on the far side of the upper walkway.

steps.text: Drop down to the lower level of that room and climb the ladder in its southwest corner.
steps.detail: The ladder puts you back on the upper level with the way through open.

steps.text: Return to the main room and cross the long bridge to the room with the Armos statues.
steps.detail: The bridge spans the main room at the upper level; the Armos room is on the far side.

steps.text: Push the Armos statue out of the way and climb the ladder behind it.
steps.detail: Walk into the statue and keep pushing until it clears the ladder. Do not hit it or it comes to life.

steps.text: Step on the switch at the top to unlock the door, then go through it into the giant staircase room.
steps.detail: The door on the far side of the Armos room clicks open while you stand on the switch and stays unlocked.

steps.text: Reach the cubby hole at the top of the staircase, kill the Gold Skulltula inside and pull the token in with the Boomerang.
steps.detail: Two ways up: go around the left side and climb the vines, or jump off the ledge above so you land on the steps themselves. The alcove is hidden at the very top of the stairs.

steps.text: Go to the House of Skulltula in Kakariko Village and talk to the cursed man who owes you 30 tokens to get the Giant's Wallet.
steps.detail: The Giant's Wallet holds 500 Rupees. If you never claimed the 10 and 20 token rewards, the people in the earlier rooms of the house still have the Adult's Wallet and the Stone of Agony waiting.

steps.text: Talk to the next cursed man in the House of Skulltula to claim the 40 token reward, a pack of Bombchus.
steps.detail: Bombchus are the wind-up bombs that run along floors and walls. You may already have some from Bombchu Bowling in the Market.

steps.text: Leave Zora's Domain through the exit tunnel and jump off the ledge at the far end down into Zora's River.
steps.detail: The tunnel is the one you came in through, behind the waterfall you opened with Zelda's Lullaby. The drop lands you in deep water and costs no hearts.

steps.text: Swim downstream to the west end of Zora's River, past the Bean Seller, and take the opening into Hyrule Field.
steps.detail: Mash B while swimming to move faster and sweep up the Rupees drifting in the current. If you skipped the two Pieces of Heart here earlier (the ledge by the waterfall to Zora's Domain and the skinny pillar mid-river), the Boomerang now reaches both from the platforms beside them.

steps.text: Cross Hyrule Field south-west to the Hyrule Castle Town drawbridge and keep walking at it until the scene starts.
steps.detail: The bridge is raised even in daylight and storm clouds pile up overhead; that is the cue, not a bug. Nothing here can hurt you.

steps.text: Watch the drawbridge scene through to the end.
steps.detail: The bridge drops, Impa gallops out carrying Zelda, and Zelda throws the Ocarina of Time into the moat as she passes. Ganondorf then rides up, questions you, blasts you and leaves. There is nothing to press.

steps.text: Jump into the moat and dive onto the Ocarina of Time glinting under the surface.
steps.detail: It sank right beside the drawbridge. Swim over the sparkle and hold A to dive onto it. The current pushes you around, so expect a couple of tries; climb out on the bank and jump back in if you drift past.

steps.text: Play the Song of Time back to Princess Zelda in the vision to learn it.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Right, A, C-Down, C-Right, A, C-Down. You come to on the bank with the drawbridge lowered. Navi wants you at the Temple of Time, but run the Happy Mask errands first.

steps.text: Cross the lowered drawbridge into the Market.
steps.detail: The town is busy again and the guards no longer turn you away.

steps.text: Go into the Happy Mask Shop, the door on the right-hand side of the square beside the stairway up to the Temple of Time.
steps.detail: The whole mask chain is optional. It needs Zelda's Letter already handed to the Death Mountain gate guard, which you did long ago.

steps.text: Talk to the Happy Mask Salesman and borrow the Keaton Mask.
steps.detail: Nothing is paid up front. Each mask has a price (the Keaton Mask is worth 10 Rupees) and you settle up after you have sold it. Only one mask is on offer at a time.

steps.text: Leave the Market, cross Hyrule Field to the north-east and climb the long stone staircase into Kakariko Village.
steps.detail: Follow the road right from the drawbridge and hug the mountain wall; the staircase is cut into the cliff at the far end.

steps.text: Walk to the back of the village and go up the steps to the Death Mountain Trail gate.
steps.detail: Past the windmill and the watchtower, at the highest point of the village.

steps.text: Put on the Keaton Mask and talk to the guard standing at the gate to sell it for 15 Rupees.
steps.detail: Same guard who read Zelda's Letter and talked your ear off about the mask he wanted for his son. Assign the mask to a C button on the item screen first; he only reacts while you are wearing it. You come out 5 Rupees ahead.

steps.text: Go back down the staircase into Hyrule Field, cross to the Market and step into the Happy Mask Shop.
Pay the salesman the 10 Rupees the Keaton Mask was worth.
steps.detail: He takes the money the moment you talk to him; the 5 Rupees you made on the sale stay in your wallet.

steps.text: Borrow the Skull Mask.
steps.detail: It is worth 20 Rupees, so that is what you owe once it is sold.

steps.text: Leave the Market and cross Hyrule Field south-west to the bridge into Kokiri Forest.
steps.detail: The bridge sits in the far corner of the field, under the big tree line. Follow the road left out of the drawbridge and keep the cliffs on your left.

steps.text: Cross Kokiri Forest to the north-west, over the little bridge past the shop, and go through the log tunnel into the Lost Woods.
steps.detail: The tunnel is the hollow log across the stream, the same way you went for Saria's Song.

steps.text: From the entrance clearing take the tunnel on the right, then in the next clearing take the tunnel on the left.
steps.detail: The full route to the back meadow is right, left, right, left, left. Saria's Song gets louder each time you pick correctly. Guess wrong and you are dumped back at the entrance, so restart the count from there.

steps.text: Take the tunnel on the right, then the tunnel on the left.
steps.detail: That is four of the five turns done.

steps.text: Take the left tunnel one more time to reach the clearing before the Sacred Forest Meadow.
steps.detail: This is the clearing with a tunnel leading on to the Meadow. Ignore that tunnel for now.

steps.text: Pace back and forth under the cloud of butterflies at the back of the clearing until you fall through the hidden hole into the Forest Stage.
steps.detail: The hole has no marking at all. Keep walking small circles under the butterflies and you will drop in.

steps.text: Put on the Skull Mask and step forward to the middle of the stage.
steps.detail: Deku Scrubs pop out of the ground, look you over and scamper around you, impressed by the mask.

steps.text: Stand still until their leader turns up and hands you the Deku Stick upgrade: you can now carry 30.
steps.detail: Moving around does not break it, but staying put is quickest.

steps.text: Step onto the glowing spot where you landed to leave the Forest Stage.
steps.detail: It puts you back in the clearing under the butterflies.

steps.text: Leave the clearing through any tunnel except the correct one so the woods dump you back at the Lost Woods entrance.
steps.detail: Quickest way home. Retracing the five turns backwards works too, but this is two screens.

steps.text: At the entrance clearing, turn left and climb onto the tree stump.
steps.detail: Same stump where the Skull Kid rewarded you for playing Saria's Song.

steps.text: With the Skull Mask on, talk to the Skull Kid on the stump to sell it for 10 Rupees.
steps.detail: He pays 10 for a mask worth 20, so this one loses you 10 Rupees. The sale is what unlocks the next mask, so there is no way around it.

steps.text: Leave the Lost Woods, cross Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field back to the Market, and go into the Happy Mask Shop.
Pay the salesman the 20 Rupees the Skull Mask was worth.
steps.detail: Turn up with at least 20 Rupees in hand; the Skull Kid only gave you 10 of them.

steps.text: Borrow the Spooky Mask.
steps.detail: It is worth 30 Rupees and looks like the face of a ReDead.

steps.text: Cross Hyrule Field to Kakariko Village and take the path up the right-hand side of the village, past the windmill, into the Graveyard.
Wearing the Spooky Mask, talk to the boy stomping around with a stick among the gravestones in the middle of the Graveyard to sell it for 30 Rupees.
steps.detail: He is only out during the day; play the Sun's Song if you arrive at night. He wants to be as frightening as Dampé the gravekeeper and pays the full 30 without haggling.

steps.text: Plant a Magic Bean in the patch of soft soil up the left-hand side of the Graveyard.
steps.detail: The soil is a small round dirt circle against the left wall. Stand on it and use a Magic Bean from a C button. Out of beans? The Bean Seller sits at the start of Zora's River and each bean costs 10 Rupees more than the last. Adult Link rides this plant to a Piece of Heart on the high ledge here.

steps.text: Head back down to Hyrule Field, into the Market and into the Happy Mask Shop.
Pay the salesman the 30 Rupees the Spooky Mask was worth.
steps.detail: This one breaks even: the boy paid exactly what you owe.

steps.text: Borrow the Bunny Hood.
steps.detail: Worth 50 Rupees, and the last mask you ever have to pay for.

steps.text: Leave the Market, follow the road to the right and keep going until you meet the Running Man on the road that circles Lon Lon Ranch.
steps.detail: He starts in the north-east corner of the field and laps it counter-clockwise, sticking to the ranch road. Coming out of the Market and walking right runs into him around the ranch.

steps.text: Wait for him to stop for a breather, playing the Sun's Song to push time along if he will not sit down.
steps.detail: He only talks while resting. He rests on the road itself, so stand where he stopped.

steps.text: Talk to him with the Bunny Hood on to sell it.
steps.detail: He has heard the hood grants unnatural speed and pays over 500 Rupees for it, far more than a child's wallet holds, so you simply cap out full. Hang around afterwards to watch him sprint off.

steps.text: Walk back to the Market and into the Happy Mask Shop one more time.
Pay the salesman the 50 Rupees the Bunny Hood was worth.
steps.detail: That settles the whole chain; you owe him nothing after this.

steps.text: Borrow the Mask of Truth.
steps.detail: Four masks unlock at once: Mask of Truth, Goron Mask, Zora Mask and Gerudo Mask. They are free and never repaid. The other three are decoration; the Mask of Truth lets you read the Gossip Stones dotted around Hyrule.

steps.text: Cross Hyrule Field to Kokiri Forest and take the log tunnel into the Lost Woods again.
From the entrance clearing take the tunnels right, left, right.
steps.detail: Same route as before: right, left, right, left, left.

steps.text: Take left, then left again, to reach the clearing before the Sacred Forest Meadow.
Drop through the hidden hole under the butterflies at the back of the clearing into the Forest Stage.
steps.detail: Same unmarked hole as the first visit; walk circles under the butterflies.

steps.text: Put on the Mask of Truth and step forward to the middle of the stage.
steps.detail: The Deku Scrubs appear, take one look and recoil in horror.

steps.text: Take the Deku Nut upgrade the terrified scrubs hand over anyway: you can now carry 40.
steps.detail: This is not the Lost Woods Business Scrub upgrade, so nothing about the adult trading sequence can take it away.

steps.text: Leave the Forest Stage, travel back to the Market and take the stairway between the Happy Mask Shop and the Potion Shop up to the temple gardens.
steps.detail: You need all three Spiritual Stones and the Ocarina of Time in your inventory before this is worth doing.

steps.text: Follow the path round the corner through the gardens and go in the front door of the Temple of Time.
steps.detail: The Gossip Stones out here can be read with the Mask of Truth on if you are curious. None of it is required.

steps.text: Walk up the aisle to the altar in front of the Door of Time.
steps.detail: The altar is the low stone block with three empty sockets, right under the sealed door at the back of the hall.

steps.text: Play the Song of Time standing at the altar.
steps.detail: C-Right, A, C-Down, C-Right, A, C-Down. The Kokiri's Emerald, Goron's Ruby and Zora's Sapphire settle into the altar and the Door of Time grinds open.

steps.text: Walk through the open Door of Time into the inner chamber.
steps.detail: The Master Sword is standing in a pedestal at the top of the short flight of steps.

steps.text: Step onto the Pedestal of Time and press A to pull out the Master Sword.
steps.detail: A scene plays: opening the door was exactly what Ganondorf needed, he follows you into the Sacred Realm and seven years pass. Nothing is lost by doing this; as an adult you can come back here and put the sword away to be a child again.

steps.text: Hear Rauru out in the blue chamber you wake up in.
steps.detail: Rauru, Sage of Light, explains that you were too young to wield the Master Sword, so your spirit slept seven years while Ganondorf took the Triforce and wrecked Hyrule. Beating him means waking the six Sages.

steps.text: Take the Light Medallion Rauru gives you.
steps.detail: It is the first of the six medallions. He sends you straight back to the Temple of Time afterwards.

steps.text: Head for the door of the Temple of Time as adult Link until Sheik stops you.
steps.detail: Link starts walking on his own; the hall is dark and empty. Sheik steps out of the shadows by the pedestal room.

steps.text: Hear Sheik out; she sends you to Kakariko Village before the Forest Temple.
steps.detail: She introduces herself as the last of the Sheikah and talks about the Sages. No song is taught here.

steps.text: Open the equipment screen and check that the Master Sword and the Hylian Shield are equipped.
steps.detail: Adult Link cannot use the Kokiri Sword, Deku Shield, Fairy Slingshot, Boomerang or Deku Sticks; Deku Nuts, Bombs and Bombchus still work. If you never picked up a Hylian Shield, the Bazaar in Kakariko Village sells one for 80 Rupees.

steps.text: Leave the Temple of Time, cross the ruined Market well clear of the ReDeads and go over the drawbridge into Hyrule Field.
steps.detail: ReDeads freeze you with a scream and then climb on for heavy damage. Run wide around them and never stop next to one; the Sun's Song paralyses any that wake up. Nothing in the Market can be done yet. The guardhouse on the left just before the bridge is now the Ghost Shop, which only matters for the Big Poe side quest much later.

steps.text: Run to Lon Lon Ranch in the middle of Hyrule Field and go in through the gate.
steps.detail: Optional from start to finish: you never need Epona to beat the game. Ingo runs the ranch now and Malon is hiding in the stable. If you never learned Epona's Song from Malon as a child, skip this whole section; after the Forest Temple you can become a child again and come back.

steps.text: Talk to Ingo at the corral in the middle of the ranch and pay him 10 Rupees for a horse ride.
steps.detail: He drops you inside the corral on a horse of his choosing.

steps.text: Ignore the horse Ingo put you on, play Epona's Song to call Epona over and climb onto her.
steps.detail: Epona's Song is C-Up, C-Left, C-Right, C-Up, C-Left, C-Right. Ingo's own horse is far too slow to ever win a race.

steps.text: Ride Epona at the two fences inside the corral and press A just before each one to jump it; the two jumps pay back 20 Rupees.
steps.detail: Approach straight on at a gallop. The carrots on the right of the screen are your sprints; they refill on their own.

steps.text: Z-target Ingo from Epona's back, accept his challenge and beat him in the first race.
steps.detail: He jumps the start and takes the corners wide. Cut the inside of every corner, save two or three carrots and spend them on the last straight. Losing only costs the entry fee, so pay again and retry.

steps.text: Take Ingo's second race, the one where he bets Epona herself, and beat him again.
steps.detail: This time he barges into you whenever you draw alongside. The simplest line is to burn carrots off the start, get clear in front and hold the inside of every corner so he can never reach you.

steps.text: Ingo locks the ranch gate; take a long run-up on Epona and jump her over the fence to get out.
steps.detail: Any of the low outer walls works. Gallop straight at it and press A a moment before you reach it. A short scene plays as she clears it, and Epona is yours for good.

steps.text: Come back into the ranch, talk to Malon from Epona's back and finish her two-lap obstacle race in under 50 seconds to win a Cow.
steps.detail: Ingo is harmless again and Malon recognises you. Jump every fence rather than going around, and keep a carrot for the second lap. The Cow turns up inside your old house in Kokiri Forest; play Epona's Song at it for free Lon Lon Milk.

steps.text: Ride east across Hyrule Field to Kakariko Village and take the path at the back of the village up into the Graveyard.
steps.detail: Call Epona with Epona's Song out in the field to cross it quickly; she waits outside while you are in the village. Sheik told you to come here, and the Hookshot you need for the Forest Temple is at the bottom of a grave.

steps.text: On the left-hand side of the Graveyard, stand on the Magic Bean plant growing out of the soft soil and ride it up to the ledge above.
steps.detail: The plant only exists if you planted a bean in this soil as a child. If the soil is bare, plant one now for 10 Rupees and come back on a later visit, once seven years of growth have happened in one time-travel.

steps.text: Roll into the wooden crate on the ledge and take the Piece of Heart inside.
steps.detail: Press A while running to roll. You can also slash the crate apart with the Master Sword.

steps.text: Back on the ground beside the bean plant, grab the grave with flowers in front of it, pull it back to uncover the hole and drop in.
steps.detail: Stand against the headstone, hold A to grab and walk backwards. This is Dampé's grave; the flowered one is the only grave here that hides a tunnel.

steps.text: Talk to Dampé's ghost to start his race, then chase him along the first stretch of tunnel by following the left-hand wall.
steps.detail: You lose if he gets too far ahead and reaches a door before you. He stops briefly at each door, so never stop to fight anything; keep running the whole way.

steps.text: After the first door, hug the right-hand wall until the tunnel opens out into a big room.
Take the right-hand exit out of the big room, then go left and right at the purple flames.
Through the next door keep to the right side, climb the ledge on the left or straight ahead, then follow the tunnel to the small room where Dampé stops.
steps.detail: The ledges are the only climb in the race; jump at them and press A to pull up. After this it is a straight run to the end.

steps.text: Open the chest Dampé leaves behind for the Hookshot.
steps.detail: Assign it to a C button now. It kills Skulltulas and Skullwalltulas in one shot from either side, pulls you to wooden targets and chests, and is what the Forest Temple is built around.

steps.text: Go through the open doorway ahead, then play the Song of Time beside the big blue Time Block to make it disappear.
steps.detail: The door shuts behind you. Song of Time is C-Right, A, C-Down, C-Right, A, C-Down. If you target the block, Navi points out that it carries the same symbols as the Temple of Time.

steps.text: Climb the ledge the block was covering and run up the stairs into the top of the Windmill.
On the walkway at the top of the Windmill, wait for a turning gear to come round to you and jump onto the spinning platform.
steps.detail: Do not jump at the gap until a platform is level with your walkway, or you drop to the windmill floor and have to climb the stairs from the Graveyard tunnel again.

steps.text: Ride the platform round to the ledge holding the Piece of Heart and hop off onto it.
steps.detail: Jump the moment the platform lines up with the ledge.

steps.text: Drop down to the windmill floor and go out the door into Kakariko Village.
steps.detail: Guru-Guru is the man cranking the organ down here; talking to him teaches the Song of Storms. You do not need it until the Bottom of the Well much later, so learn it now or leave it, whichever you prefer.

steps.text: Go back up to the Graveyard, drop into Dampé's grave again and talk to him for a rematch.
steps.detail: The tunnel is the same route you just ran; only the prize changes.

steps.text: Beat the race in one minute or less so Dampé digs up a Piece of Heart at the finish.
steps.detail: Same route as before. Cut every corner, never stop for enemies, take the ledge climbs at a run and use the tunnel walls to guide you rather than the camera. Anything over a minute just gets you Rupees, so leave the tunnel and talk to him again for another try.

steps.text: Pick the Piece of Heart up off the ground before you go anywhere else.
steps.detail: He digs it out right where he stops; walk over it.
steps.missable: Take it the instant he digs it up. If you leave the tunnel with the Piece of Heart still lying on the ground, the game counts it as collected and you can never get it again.

steps.text: Down in the village, stand outside the Windmill door and jump onto the fence directly ahead of it.
From the fence, Hookshot onto the roof of the building to the right and talk to the man sitting up there for a Piece of Heart.
steps.detail: Aim the Hookshot at the roof edge; the fence gives you just enough height to reach it.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to make it night, go to the south end of the village beside Impa's House and Hookshot up onto the roof of the House of Skulltula.
steps.detail: Sun's Song is C-Right, C-Down, C-Up, C-Right, C-Down, C-Up. The House of Skulltula is the building with the spider design by the village entrance; Impa's House is the tall one next to it.

steps.text: Hookshot across to the roof of Impa's House, kill the Gold Skulltula waiting there and take its token.
steps.detail: Night only. The Hookshot kills it and reels in the token in one shot.

steps.text: Go back to the Market and take the north gate up the path to what is left of Hyrule Castle, now Ganon's Castle.
steps.detail: Nothing else up here can be done yet; the castle itself is unreachable across the chasm.

steps.text: Follow the path to the right past the stone archway, turn around and Hookshot the Gold Skulltula clinging to the back of the arch for its token.
steps.detail: It is invisible from the approach; you only see it once you have gone past and looked back.

steps.text: Cross Hyrule Field to the south-east corner and go through the tunnel into Kokiri Forest.
steps.detail: The forest is overrun. Big Deku Babas fight exactly like the small ones, they are just tall enough that your slashes often miss; back off, let one lunge and cut it as it comes down. The Kokiri are shut in their houses and do not recognise you.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song to make it night and walk over to the Twins' House in the south-east part of the forest.
steps.detail: Listen for the Gold Skulltula's rattle; it gets louder as you close in.

steps.text: Hookshot the Gold Skulltula on the wall above the Twins' House and take its token.
Climb the vines up to the log tunnel at the top of the village and go through into the Lost Woods.
From the first clearing, take the tunnel on the right.
steps.detail: Every wrong tunnel drops you back at the Kokiri Forest entrance, so count your turns. The full route from here is right, left, right, left, straight, left, right.

steps.text: Take the tunnel on the left.
Take the tunnel on the right; Mido is standing in the way at the far end.
steps.detail: He is the only Kokiri outside and he refuses to believe you know Saria.

steps.text: Play Saria's Song so Mido steps aside, then take the tunnel on the left.
steps.detail: Saria's Song is C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left. He gives up as soon as he hears it.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song for night, then stand on the Magic Bean plant in this clearing and ride it up to the ledge at the top.
steps.detail: Only there if you planted a bean in this soft soil as a child. If the soil is bare, plant one and come back after your next trip through time, or skip ahead and fetch this Skulltula on a later visit.

steps.text: Slash the Gold Skulltula on the wall up there and Hookshot in its token.
steps.detail: Without the bean plant you can still send a Bombchu up the wall to blow it off, then reel the token in with the Hookshot.

steps.text: Carry straight on through the next clearing, then take the left tunnel, then the right one, and you come out at the Sacred Forest Meadow.
steps.detail: Three turns in a row with no branches worth exploring: straight, left, right.

steps.text: Work up the first corridors of the hedge maze, dropping the Moblins from behind one at a time as you move from alcove to alcove.
steps.detail: Each Moblin walks a fixed patrol and only charges if it actually sees you. Duck into the side alcoves, wait for one to turn away, then Hookshot it or run up and slash. Bombs bounced off a wall work too.

steps.text: Wade the two pools at the far end of the maze, waiting out the Moblin that patrols the L-shaped corner before you climb out.
steps.detail: You are slow and exposed in the water, so stay in one pool until that Moblin has walked the long leg of its route away from you.

steps.text: Fight the Club Moblin guarding the steps at the end of the maze.
steps.detail: He swings a huge club and stamps the ground. Zig-zag in so the shockwaves miss, then hack at his feet; he topples after a few hits and leaves a pile of Rupees. Backflip out whenever he raises the club.

steps.text: Go up the steps to Saria's stump and watch Sheik's scene.
Learn the Minuet of Forest from Sheik.
steps.detail: A, C-Up, C-Left, C-Right, C-Left, C-Right. It warps you to the entrance of the Sacred Forest Meadow from anywhere, so you never have to run the Lost Woods again.

steps.text: Play the Sun's Song for night and climb the ladder at the end of the meadow up to the high ledge.
steps.detail: The ladder is on the wall beside the temple steps.

steps.text: Work along the ledge to the left, look up at the east wall and Hookshot the Gold Skulltula for its token.
steps.detail: Night only. If you have already gone into the temple, warp back with the Minuet of Forest, run the maze again and kill the Club Moblin, who respawns.

steps.text: Save your game, Hookshot the tree branch hanging above the temple steps to pull yourself up, and walk into the Forest Temple.
steps.detail: Aim at the branch, not the doorway. Stock up on Deku Nuts and keep a bottled Fairy if you have one; the Stalfos inside hit hard.

steps.text: Fight the two Wolfos in the entrance courtyard.
steps.detail: Z-target one and the other leaves you alone. Wait for it to swipe, sidestep or backflip, then cut its tail: a jump attack from behind kills a Wolfos outright. Doors with the forest symbol above them lead deeper into the temple; plain doors lead back.

steps.text: Climb the vines on the right-hand wall of the courtyard to the top.
Step across onto the treetop on your left and Hookshot the Gold Skulltula on the vines for its token.
steps.detail: From the top of the tree you can see it hanging on the vine wall you just climbed.

steps.text: Walk along the branches to the second treetop and open the chest up there for a Small Key.
steps.detail: Take the branches slowly; falling just means climbing the vines again.

steps.text: Drop back down and go through the door at the back of the courtyard.
Hookshot the big Skulltula hanging in the hallway, then go through the door at the end into the Grand Hall.
steps.detail: The Hookshot kills a Skulltula in one hit from either side, front shell included. A scene plays as you enter: the four Poe Sisters lift the flames off the torches and scatter into the corners of the temple.

steps.text: Cross the Grand Hall to the far side, climb the ledge and go up the steps to the north door.
steps.detail: This central room is the hub; almost every route comes back here. The round platform in the middle of the floor is a dead elevator that only works once all four Poes are gone.

steps.text: Before going through, Hookshot the Gold Skulltula on the wall just to the right of the north door for its token.
Go through the north door, kill the Blue Bubble in the short hallway and take the far door, the one with the forest symbol above it.
steps.detail: A Blue Bubble is a flaming skull that your sword cannot touch while it burns. Knock the flame out with a shield bash or the Hookshot, then slash it.

steps.text: Beat the two Stalfos that lock you in.
steps.detail: They hit for a full heart and block most sword swings. Z-target one at a time, hold your shield up as you close, backflip the moment it jumps, and stab in the gap right after it lands. Deku Nuts stun both at once if you get surrounded.

steps.text: Open the chest that appears for the second Small Key.
Smash the jars in the corner and catch the Fairy in an empty bottle.
steps.detail: Swing at the jar, then hold the empty bottle out at the Fairy. A bottled Fairy revives you once when you die, which is worth having before Phantom Ganon.

steps.text: Go back through the hallway to the Grand Hall and play the Song of Time beside the blue Time Block standing in front of the northwest door.
steps.detail: The northwest door is on the same upper level, to the left of the north door as you face out into the hall.

steps.text: Go through the northwest door into the open-air Ruins.
Kill the Big Deku Baba right inside the door, then follow the ledge to the right as far as the vine-covered wall.
steps.detail: You can also just walk around the Baba; it cannot leave its root.

steps.text: Hookshot the two lower Skullwalltulas off the vines.
steps.detail: Skullwalltulas are the small spiders crawling on the vines; touching one knocks you off.

steps.text: Climb the vines along their right-hand edge to squeeze past the top Skullwalltula, then go through the door at the top.
steps.detail: Hug the far right of the vine wall and climb steadily. If it knocks you off, climb again as soon as it crawls upward.

steps.text: Kill the lone Blue Bubble in the Map Room; a big chest drops in.
Open the big chest for the Dungeon Map.
Go through the far door, the one with the symbol above it, out into the northeast Ruins.
Kill the Deku Baba on the path, then Hookshot the symbol on the wall above the raised platform to pull yourself up onto it.
steps.detail: Aim at the painted symbol, not the platform; it lands you safely on top.

steps.text: Step on the switch on the platform. The water drains out of the courtyard below and out of the well with it.
steps.detail: The pool below and the one in the open-air room you came through are the same body of water.

steps.text: Drop down into the drained pool and climb out onto the dry ground.
Hookshot the long side of the small chest sitting on the ledge above the water to pull yourself up to it.
steps.detail: Aim at the face of the chest, not the lid. The Hookshot reels you onto the ledge.

steps.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula just around the corner from the chest and Hookshot in its token.
Climb down into the well and open the chest at the far end for the third Small Key.
steps.detail: The well is the shaft in the middle of the courtyard; it is only enterable now that the water is gone.

steps.text: Climb out of the well on either side and work back through the Ruins and the northwest door to the Grand Hall.
Open the locked door on the west side of the Grand Hall with a Small Key.
steps.detail: It is on the lower floor, to the left as you look back at the entrance hallway. You have three keys and nothing else needs them yet.

steps.text: Hookshot the Skulltula hanging in the west hallway, then go through the candle-lit door at the end into the Block Room.
steps.detail: The Block Room is the tall shaft with coloured blocks and ladders; you will be up and down it several times.

steps.text: Kill the Blue Bubble that comes at you as you walk in.
steps.detail: Shield bash or Hookshot to put its flame out, then slash.

steps.text: Climb the two ladders straight ahead, round the corner, then pull the blue block out until it lines up with the corner of the wall.
steps.detail: Grab the block with A and walk backwards. Arrows painted on the floor show the directions it can move. Get this first pull right and the rest of the puzzle falls into place.

steps.text: Go round to the left side of the blue block and push it all the way back along the arrow.
Walk around through the doorway the block just uncovered and push the blue block once more, until it clicks into its hole in the floor.
steps.detail: The click means it is seated; it now works as a step up to the next level.

steps.text: Go back and climb the ladder the block uncovered, then round the corner to the red block.
Push the red block until it stops against the wall.
Go back down the ladder, climb on top of the blue block and jump to the ledge tucked away on the right.
steps.detail: It is easy to miss: from the top of the blue block, turn right and the ledge is almost level with you.

steps.text: Round the corner to the red block again and push it until it clicks into place.
Kill the two Blue Bubbles on this upper level.
steps.detail: There is a silver eye switch above the door up here. You cannot do anything with it until you have the Bow, which is where you are going now.

steps.text: Open the locked door on this level with a Small Key.
Walk through the twisted corridor behind it.
steps.detail: The whole corridor has been rolled onto its side, so you walk along what should be a wall. Nothing in here can hurt you.

steps.text: In the crooked room at the end, jump to the next platform, turn right and jump again to the door, keeping ahead of the Wallmaster.
steps.detail: A Wallmaster is the giant hand that drops out of the ceiling onto your shadow. Being caught costs a heart and dumps you back at the temple entrance, so never stand still in this room.

steps.text: Go down the stairs in Joelle's room and out through the door at the bottom.
steps.detail: This is the room of laughing portraits. You can hear the Poe but you cannot touch her until you have the Bow, so ignore it for now.

steps.text: Beat the Stalfos in the Bow Room; a floating platform comes down and fills the pit in the middle.
steps.detail: Do not fall in the pit: it drops you back into the Stalfos room in the north wing and you have to walk the whole west wing again. Fight along the outer ring of floor.

steps.text: Beat the two Stalfos that appear on the new floor.
steps.detail: Kill the second one quickly or the first comes straight back. Hold your shield up, backflip their jump attacks and stab between their swings. A bottled Fairy is worth having ready.

steps.text: Open the big chest for the Fairy Bow.
steps.detail: Put it on a C button. Arrows are fired with Z-targeting or first person; press R for the shield if something closes on you while you are aiming.

steps.text: Go back up through Joelle's room, across the crooked room and along the twisted corridor to the top level of the Block Room.
steps.detail: Same route as before, in reverse: out of the Bow Room, up the stairs in Joelle's room, across the two platforms past the Wallmaster, through the corridor.

steps.text: Shoot the silver eye switch above the door up here with an arrow.
steps.detail: Z-target the eye, or aim in first person. The eye snaps shut when it is hit.

steps.text: Go back through that door: the twisted corridor has straightened out.
steps.detail: Hitting the eye rolls the whole corridor upright, which opens a route that was sideways before.

steps.text: Follow the straight corridor into the crooked room, now the right way up, and jump down to the big chest.
steps.detail: The Wallmaster is still overhead; land, open, leave.

steps.text: Open the big chest for the Boss Key.
Jump down the hole in the floor beside the chest and kill the two Blue Bubbles in the room below to open its door.
steps.detail: You could climb the ladder back up, but the hole is where you need to go next.

steps.text: Go through the door into the northwest Ruins, the open-air room with the drained pool.
Jump out onto the narrow pillars with the Recovery Hearts standing on them.
steps.detail: Line the jump up carefully; missing just drops you into the empty pool, which you can climb out of.

steps.text: From the pillar, kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall above you and Hookshot in its token.
Kill the Big Deku Baba blocking the ledge ahead, then check the last alcove on the right for a door hidden in the shadows.
steps.detail: Arrows kill the Baba from a safe distance. The door is easy to walk straight past; it is set back in the darkest alcove on that side.

steps.text: Beat the Floormaster in the small room.
steps.detail: It creeps along the floor and grabs you. Z-target, walk in behind your shield, then slash the moment after it lunges. When it is nearly dead it splits into three small ones that try to merge: charge a spin attack while it is dying and release it to wipe out all three at once.

steps.text: Open the small chest that drops in for another Small Key.
Go back out and take the door on the right, the shortcut straight into the Block Room.
steps.detail: It saves climbing the vines and crossing the ruins again.

steps.text: Climb back up to the blue block, shoot the eye switch across the wide open area with an arrow, then jump over and open the chest that appears for arrows.
steps.detail: The eye is on the far wall of the open section on the blue block's level. Purely a bonus, but free arrows before the boss are welcome.

steps.text: Climb to the very top of the Block Room and shoot the silver eye switch above the door again to twist the corridor back.
steps.detail: Shooting a closed eye reopens it and undoes the change, which is exactly what you want: the sideways corridor is the way to the Poe Sisters.

steps.text: Go through the door and the twisted corridor again, then jump the two platforms in the crooked room to the door on your right.
steps.detail: Keep moving: the Wallmaster is still up there.

steps.text: In Joelle's room, shoot the Poe with the Fairy Bow in each of the three portraits.
steps.detail: Walking up to a frame makes her jump to one of the other two, so watch which frame lights up and shoot from a distance. The middle level gives the best view of all three. Three hits and she comes out.

steps.text: Fight Joelle down on the floor of the room.
steps.detail: She fights like a Graveyard Poe: keep your shield up, and hit her with sword or arrows every time she drops her guard. When she vanishes, a Deku Nut brings her straight back. Five good hits and she burns out, relighting every red torch in the temple.

steps.text: Pick up the arrows she drops and open the chest that appears for a Small Key.
Go through the door, cross the Bow Room and take the far door into Beth's room.
steps.detail: The Bow Room is empty now; the pit is still filled in.

steps.text: Shoot the Poe out of all three portraits in Beth's room the same way.
Fight Beth on the lower floor; when she burns out, every blue torch in the temple lights.
steps.detail: Same fight as Joelle: shield up, five clean hits, Deku Nut if she goes invisible.

steps.text: Open the locked door at the top of Beth's room with a Small Key.
Cross the east crooked room past its Wallmaster and climb the ladder up to the hallway on the right.
steps.detail: Another room turned on its side, with another hand in the ceiling. You can jump straight across the gap or drop to the bottom and take the ladder; either way, do not linger.

steps.text: Walk the hallway past the Green Bubbles and open the locked door at the far end with your last Small Key.
steps.detail: Green Bubbles just loop in circles and lose their flames from time to time. Walking around them is easier than fighting them.

steps.text: In the lava room, jump onto one of the platforms moving across the middle.
steps.detail: Wait for one to come level with the ledge before you jump.

steps.text: Shoot the silver eye switch on the far platform with an arrow fired through the torch in the middle of the room.
steps.detail: The flame lights the arrow on the way past, and only a burning arrow melts that switch. Line it up from the opposite side so torch and eye are in a straight line. If you have Din's Fire, you can instead ride onto the switch's platform and cast it.

steps.text: Go back into the east crooked room, now twisted round, and drop down the hole that has opened in it.
steps.detail: Melting the eye rolled that room over and exposed the hole.

steps.text: In the Checkerboard Room, wait for the ceiling to come down so you can read the safe squares, then work your way across to the switch at the far end.
steps.detail: The camera locks to a side-on view here: no Z-targeting, and aiming a weapon only swings it around while you keep moving. Squares with a shadow on them drop a Skulltula on you. Hold the Hookshot button down and release it as you come alongside one to clear the square.

steps.text: Step on the switch; it unlocks the door on the other side of the room. Go through it into Amy's room.
Shoot the big picture of Amy with an arrow; five blocks drop out of the ceiling.
steps.detail: Stay off the shadows on the floor first, or a Skulltula lands on you mid-puzzle. You get one minute and ten seconds once the blocks land; leaving the room and coming back resets the whole puzzle, and the first arrangement is the easiest one.

steps.text: Shove the odd blue block in the middle out of the way.
Push and pull the other four blocks together to finish the picture before the timer runs out.
steps.detail: Pick one block, leave it where it is and drag the other three to it; that saves the most time. Grab with A and walk.

steps.text: Fight Amy the same way as her sisters; the door beside her opens and her flame is lit.
steps.detail: Shield up, five hits, Deku Nut when she disappears.

steps.text: Go through the opened door, Hookshot the Skulltula in the hallway and take the door at the end out onto the Grand Hall ledge.
Jump down from the ledge to the floor of the Grand Hall and walk up to Meg in the middle of the room.
steps.detail: Nothing on the ledge is worth stopping for. Meg is the last Poe Sister, drifting around the hub.

steps.text: Beat Meg.
steps.detail: She splits into four copies and swipes at you for half a heart if you guess wrong. Spin attacks, Deku Nuts and Din's Fire do nothing to her. Stand still, let them spin, and watch: the real Meg spins one extra time at the end. Z-target that one and shoot it. Five hits finish her.

steps.text: Smash the pots around the hall for arrows and hearts, then stand on the round platform in the middle of the floor and ride the elevator down to the basement.
steps.detail: With all four Poe flames back on the torches, the elevator finally works.

steps.text: Push one of the two big handles to turn the room counter-clockwise once, then step on the switch in the white-floored alcove it opens up.
steps.detail: Turning the wall swings different alcoves into the room. Always turn counter-clockwise and the four steps come in the order white switch, red switch, chest, blue switch. The barred hallway on one side is the way to the boss.

steps.text: Turn the room counter-clockwise again and step on the switch in the red-floored alcove.
Turn the room counter-clockwise again; this time the alcove has a treasure chest in it.
Open the chest for the Compass.
Kill the Gold Skulltula in the same alcove and take its token.
steps.detail: The last one in the temple. The Hookshot gets it and the token in one shot.

steps.text: Turn the room counter-clockwise one last time and step on the switch in the blue-floored alcove; the bars over the hallway to the boss lift.
steps.detail: All four switches are now pressed, so the way forward stays open.

steps.text: Top up arrows, hearts and a bottled Fairy, save your game, then follow the hallway and walk up the ramp into the boss arena.
